title: Radiomics performance to identify high-risk carotid artery plaques: a systematic review.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Stroke is a leading cause of mortality worldwide, with 15-20% of ischemic strokes caused by extracranial carotid atherosclerotic disease. Risk stratification has traditionally relied on luminal stenosis severity, which inadequately reflects plaque vulnerability. Radiomics offers an emerging solution by extracting high-dimensional quantitative data from standard medical images. This systematic review evaluated the performance of radiomics-based models for identifying high-risk carotid plaques. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A systematic search was conducted across multiple databases. Studies were included if they developed or validated radiomics-based models for carotid plaque assessment and reported performance metrics, specifically the area under the curve (AUC). Data were extracted on study design, imaging modalities, segmentation methods, and modeling techniques. RESULTS: Twenty-eight studies involving 6,108 patients (72.4% male) were included. Computed tomography angiography was the most commonly used imaging modality (n = 16), and manual region-of-interest segmentation was performed in 27 of 28 studies. Radiomics models showed strong predictive performance. Internal validation AUCs were as high as 0.984, whereas combined models incorporating radiomics with clinical and/or conventional radiological features achieved the best predictive accuracy, often exceeding 0.90. However, only four studies included external validation cohorts. CONCLUSION: Radiomics is a powerful, non-invasive tool for identifying high-risk carotid plaques, offering superior discriminative power over conventional stenosis-based assessments. Despite these promising results, the field faces significant hurdles, and future research must prioritize prospective multicenter trials, the development of automated segmentation workflows, and the correlation of radiomic features with histopathological findings to ensure clinical reproducibility and transition into routine stroke prevention. KEY POINTS: Question Standard carotid atherosclerotic disease assessments fail to capture biological plaque complexity and vulnerability, necessitating objective, reproducible, and non-invasive methods to improve stroke prevention. Findings Radiomics and combined models demonstrate superior capability in identifying high-risk carotid plaques compared to traditional assessments. With four external validations, the field remains exploratory. Relevance statement Radiomics offers a non-invasive tool for personalized stroke prevention. However, technical barriers currently prevent its transition to routine clinical use, including reliance on manual segmentation and low compliance with international standardization guidelines.

title: Characterization of Perfusion Scotoma in Acute Ischemic Stroke after Endovascular Treatment.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: CTP may underestimate the size of the ischemic core, a phenomenon known as perfusion scotoma. We aimed to investigate the prevalence of perfusion scotoma, characterize its baseline predictors, and explore its association with functional outcomes in a real-world population of patients with stroke treated with endovascular treatment (EVT). MATERIALS AND METHODS: P Data were obtained from a prospective EVT registry, selecting patients with successful recanaliztion (final modified TICI ≥2b), a good-quality baseline CTP, and an available 24-hour noncontrast CT. Ischemic core underestimated volume (ICuV) was calculated as the difference between follow-up infarct volume and CTP-estimated ischemic core. The primary outcome was the presence of perfusion scotoma, defined as ICuV ≥10 mL. Baseline characteristics withvalue <.20 in univariable comparisons were entered in a backward stepwise, multivariable logistic regression analysis to identify factors independently associated with perfusion scotoma. RESULTS: P P P P A total of 464 patients of 672 (69%) were included in the analysis. The median age was 74 years (interquartile range = 68-83), 215 (46.3%) were men, and 116 (25%) had a perfusion scotoma. Perfusion scotoma was independently associated with male sex (adjusted OR 1.62 [95% CI, 1.01-2.51];= .04), more distal site of occlusion (adjusted OR 1.60 [95% CI, 1.10-2.34];= .01; per each 1-point increase: terminal ICA to M1 to M2), lower ASPECTS at admission (adjusted OR 0.64 [95% CI, 0.54-0.76];< .001; per each 1-point increase), and longer onset-to-CT time (adjusted OR 1.05, [95% CI, 1.01-1.10];= .03; per each 1-hour increase). The optimal onset-to-CT time cutoff to distinguish between patients without and with perfusion scotoma was 420 minutes. Perfusion scotoma was associated with 90-day ordinal mRS (adjusted common OR 3.16 [95% CI, 2.12-4.76]). CONCLUSIONS: Perfusion scotoma occurred in 1 of every 4 patients. Baseline predictors included male sex, lower ASPECTS, more distal vessel occlusion, and longer onset-to-CT time. Perfusion scotoma was associated with poorer functional outcomes.

title: Age-specific associations of endovascular therapy and reperfusion delay with outcomes after large vessel occlusion: a regional registry study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: The benefit of endovascular therapy (EVT) in very elderly patients with large vessel occlusion (LVO) remains uncertain, and sensitivity to reperfusion delay may differ by age. We evaluated age-specific associations of treatment and reperfusion time with functional outcomes. PATIENTS AND METHODS: We analysed 1,280 patients with acute LVO in an emergency medical service-based registry, divided into groups aged 85 years or older and younger than 85 years. The primary outcome was an ordinal shift towards a better 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score. Secondary outcomes were dichotomized functional measures incorporating prestroke status. RESULTS: Among 837 patients younger than 85 years, EVT was associated with a favourable mRS shift (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.47; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.07-2.01). Among 443 patients aged 85 years or older, the estimate was favourable but not statistically significant (aOR, 1.29; 95% CI, 0.87-1.92). No significant age-by-treatment interaction was observed for functional outcomes. Among patients treated with successful reperfusion by EVT, favourable outcomes declined more steeply with increasing onset-to-reperfusion time in those aged 85 years or older. DISCUSSION: The association of EVT with functional outcomes was not significantly modified by age but estimates in very elderly patients were less precise. Very elderly patients appeared more vulnerable to reperfusion delay. CONCLUSION: Treatment selection should integrate prestroke function, stroke severity, imaging findings, procedural feasibility, and the likelihood of rapid reperfusion rather than age alone.

title: The Latest Progress in the Application of Tofacitinib in Rheumatic Diseases--A Narrative Review.
abstract: Tofacitinib is an oral Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor that modulates cytokine-dependent JAK/STAT signaling and has been extensively investigated in rheumatic diseases. This narrative review provides an updated synthesis of the pharmacological characteristics, mechanisms of action, clinical efficacy, safety, drug-drug interactions and dosing considerations of tofacitinib in special populations. The relevant literature published from January 2013 through December 2025 was identified through searches of MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar, supplemented by manual screening of reference lists. After screening and eligibility assessment, 89 clinical publications were included in the disease-specific evidence synthesis, and the strength of clinical evidence across disease indications was evaluated qualitatively. The most robust evidence is available for rheumatoid arthritis, with randomized trials, long-term extension studies, and real-world investigations demonstrating improvements in disease activity and physical function and inhibition of radiographic progression. Clinical evidence also supports therapeutic benefit in psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, and juvenile idiopathic arthritis, whereas evidence for Takayasu arteritis, polymyalgia rheumatica, systemic lupus erythematosus, and anti-MDA5-positive dermatomyositis-associated interstitial lung disease remains limited or exploratory. Long-term integrated safety analyses in RA have reported incidence rates of serious adverse events of approximately 9.0-9.4 per 100 patient-years and serious infections of approximately 2.5-2.7 per 100 patient-years, while herpes zoster, major adverse cardiovascular events, venous thromboembolism, and malignancy remain clinically important safety considerations. Potential drug-drug interactions and dose adjustment in patients with renal or hepatic impairment and other special populations further require individualized assessment. Overall, tofacitinib has a well-established role in RA treatment and potential therapeutic value in several other rheumatic diseases; however, its use should be guided by disease-specific evidence, previous treatment exposure, comorbidities, concomitant medications, and individual safety risks. Further prospective and long-term studies are needed to better define its role in less well-established indications and special populations.

title: Electrosurgical Septotomy Across the Full Spectrum of Aortic Dissection.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Transcatheter electrosurgical septotomy divides the dissection membrane to reconstitute a single aortic lumen. Reported experience is largely confined to chronic post-dissection aneurysms. We assessed the technique across the full spectrum of descending aortic dissection, including stand-alone treatment of malperfusion. METHODS: A retrospective intention-to-treat analysis of 21 consecutive patients scheduled for septotomy between June 2022 and May 2026. The membrane was crossed by needle re-entry and divided with an electrified through-and-through guidewire at 40-60 W under fluoroscopy, without routine intravascular ultrasound or image fusion. A perfused-lumen index (perfused lumen divided by total aortic diameter) was measured before and after the procedure. RESULTS: Septotomy was performed in 20 of 21 patients (technical success 95% on an intention-to-treat basis). Indications were landing-zone preparation (57%), malperfusion (33%), preparation for open repair, and true-lumen collapse. Malperfusion resolved in all 7 patients treated for that indication, and the perfused-lumen index rose from a median of 0.16 to 0.98 (18 patients, P < .001). There was no stroke, spinal cord ischaemia, or retrograde type A dissection. Thirty-day, in-hospital, and overall mortality were 10%, 14%, and 19%, respectively, with 1 fatal delayed aortic rupture and no intraprocedural death. Three unplanned reinterventions occurred; median follow-up was 5.1 months. CONCLUSIONS: Electrosurgical septotomy was feasible across the full spectrum of aortic dissection and, in selected patients, as stand-alone treatment for malperfusion, using standard electrosurgical equipment. Given the small, heterogeneous cohort and short follow-up, these findings demonstrate feasibility rather than durability.

Reported experience is largely confined to chronic post-dissection aneurysms. title: Nomogram for Postoperative Permanent Neurologic Dysfunction Following Acute Type A Aortic Dissection Surgery: A Multicentral Retrospective Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Permanent neurologic dysfunction (PND) often complicates following surgery for acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) and is strongly correlated with unfavorable outcomes. Consequently, developing an effective diagnostic method to identify high-risk patients is of considerable importance. METHODS: This retrospective study, covering 2022 to 2024 across two centers, ultimately included 117 ATAAD patients with Supra-Aortic Branch Vessel (SABV) dissection from our center (2022-2023) as the training set and 52 ATAAD patients with SABV dissection from a secondary center (2024) as the validation set. We used logistic regression to identify predictors and developed a nomogram, which was assessed using the area under the ROC curve, calibration and decision curve analysis. External validation was conducted using the validation set. RESULTS: In this study, 169 cases were finally collected (117 in the training set and 52 in the validation set), of whom 64 patients developed postoperative PND. Four risk factors were identified: brachiocephalic trunk dissection at the bifurcation plane, chronic kidney disease, age over 50, and cross-clamp duration over 168 min. The AUC was 0.809 for the training set and 0.736 for the validation set. The nomogram model demonstrated acceptable predictive performance, and decision curve analysis potential clinical utility for predicting postoperative PND risk for thresholds of 1%-90% in the training set and 3%-75% in the validation set. CONCLUSIONS: This study developed and validated a predictive model for assessing the risk of postoperative PND in patients undergoing ATAAD surgery, which may assist clinicians in individualized risk assessment.

title: Development of Aortic Stents from Open Surgery to Endovascular Therapy: A Brazilian Contribution to the Treatment of Aortic Diseases.
abstract: The treatment of aortic diseases has undergone profound transformation over the last decades, with the progressive incorporation of endovascular techniques either replacing or complementing conventional open surgical repair. The development of aortic stents represents one of the most significant milestones in this transition. This article reviews the historical, experimental, and clinical evolution of aortic stents, with emphasis on pioneering Brazilian contributions, including the experimental phase in animal models, the first clinical applications in aortic dissection, and the role of the national industry in the development and dissemination of these technologies. The impact of these innovations on contemporary cardiovascular surgical practice and future perspectives are also discussed.

title: State of Art of Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation for the Treatment of Aortic Stenosis in Low-Risk Patients: A Perspective on Brazilian Contributions and Implementation Challenges.
abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has profoundly changed the management of severe aortic stenosis (AS), evolving from a treatment reserved for inoperable and high-risk patients to an established therapeutic option across a wide surgical risk spectrum. Although the expansion of TAVI indications has been largely supported by randomized clinical trials conducted in high-income countries, real-world experience and technological contributions from distinct healthcare systems are increasingly relevant. Brazil has played a significant role in the early adoption, structured implementation, and clinical evaluation of TAVI in Latin America. Since the first procedures performed in 2008, Brazilian centers have developed Heart Team models, contributed to national and regional registries, and generated real-world evidence demonstrating procedural safety and effectiveness comparable to international benchmarks, despite the presence of resource limitations and a higher prevalence of complex clinical and anatomical scenarios. The incorporation of TAVI into the Brazilian public health system in 2022 marked a major milestone in expanding access to minimally invasive therapy for patients with severe AS. In parallel, Brazilian scientific societies have adapted international guideline recommendations to local practice, supporting evidence-based patient selection across different surgical risk categories. Notably, Brazil has also emerged as a developer of locally engineered transcatheter valve technologies, highlighting its transition from a technology consumer to an active contributor in the field of structural heart disease. This review summarizes the historical evolution, national experience, clinical outcomes, guideline integration, technological innovation, and health economic considerations of TAVI in Brazil.

title: Snare-Assisted Traction Technique for Renal Artery Reconstruction in Endovascular Repair of Complex Thoracoabdominal Aortic Aneurysms.
abstract: Renal artery (RA) reconstruction during complex endovascular aortic repair often fails in hostile anatomy because of inadequate guidewire support. We describe snare-assisted traction (SAT), a novel endovascular bailout technique using conventional off-the-shelf devices. By combining distal snare traction with a long femoral sheath, SAT shifts target vessel reconstruction from simple wire guidance to sheath-based structural support. This provides robust stability for wire exchange and stent delivery without requiring specialized, unavailable tools or high-morbidity open conversion. Among 12 patients with severe RA angulation, ostial stenosis, or sac origin, SAT achieved 100% technical success without procedural complications. At median 6-month follow-up, all reconstructed RAs remained patent with stable renal function. SAT offers a safe, reproducible, and universally accessible solution for hostile target vessel access, significantly enhancing the feasibility and clinical safety of complex endovascular repair.

title: [Efficacy of percutaneous mechanical thrombectomy combined with transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt for acute non-cirrhotic portal vein thrombosis].
abstract: Objective: Methods: Results: Conclusions: M t t CI CI HR CI P HR CI P HR CI P P vs. t P To evaluate the efficacy of percutaneous mechanical thrombectomy combined with transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (PMT-TIPS) in patients with acute non-cirrhotic portal vein thrombosis (NCPVT).This is a retrospective case series study. The clinical data of 61 patients with acute NCPVT who underwent PMT combined with TIPS at Department of Endovascular Surgery, the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University between June 2017 and June 2023 were retrospectively analyzed. There were 39 males and 22 females, with an age ((IQR)) of 49.0 (24.5)years (range:21 to 73 years). Paired sample-test or Wilcoxon signed-rank test were used to compare liver volume and biochemical parameters before treatment and at 1 year after treatment. Independent sample-test was used to compare changes in liver volume between patients with different stent patency statuses. Kaplan-Meier analysis was used to estimate stent patency and symptom recurrence. Univariate and multivariate Cox proportional hazards regression models were used to analyze the factors associated with stent occlusion.Among the 61 patients, 7 (11.5%) died during hospitalization and 5 (8.2%) died within 30 days after discharge, most commonly due to bowel necrosis. The remaining 49 patients were followed up for 43 (34) months (range:4 to 94 months). During follow-up, stent occlusion occurred in 35 patients (71.4%), with a median primary patency of 13.0 months (95%: 7.3 to 18.7 months). Among the 35 patients with primary stent occlusion, 21 developed symptom recurrence, whereas symptom recurrence occurred in 4 of the 14 patients with sustained patency. Ten patients with stent occlusion underwent stent recanalization, with a median secondary patency of 21.0 months (95%: 16.8 to 25.2 months). Univariate Cox regression analysis showed that myeloproliferative neoplasms (=3.08, 95%: 1.48 to 6.42,=0.003) and dual-stent implantation (=2.26, 95%: 1.09 to 4.70,=0.036) were associated with an increased risk of stent occlusion; multivariate Cox regression further revealed that only myeloproliferative neoplasms (=2.75, 95%: 1.31 to 5.78,=0.008) was an independent risk factor. At one year post-procedure, inflammatory and coagulation markers improved, total liver volume decreased compared with baseline (=0.005), and the reduction in liver volume was greater in patients with patent stents than in those with stent occlusion ((-215.6±205.5)cm³(-3.5±236.5) cm³,=-3.505,=0.001).In patients with acute NCPVT, the PMT-TIPS technique is feasible, but long-term stent patency is limited. title: [Dominant false lumen flow and abnormally high shear stress: a hemodynamic analysis of multichanneled aortic dissection].
abstract: Objective: Methods: Results: Conclusions: To explore the hemodynamic characteristics of multichanneled aortic dissection (MCAD).This is a retrospective cohort study. Patients with acute uncomplicated Stanford-type B aortic dissection who presented at Zhongshan Hospital, Fudan University between January 2019 and December 2023 were enrolled. Patients were diagnosed as having either double-channeled aortic dissection (DCAD) or MCAD based on preoperative standardized computed-tomography angiography (CTA). Centered on 4 MCAD cases with preprocedural death, 4 non-preprocedural-death MCAD patients and 4 non-preprocedural-death DCAD patients with balanced baseline characteristics, complete preoperative CTA datasets and well-defined outcomes were matched, yielding a total of 12 male patients. The ages of patients in preprocedural-death MCAD group, non-preprocedural-death MCAD group and non-preprocedural- death DCAD group were (62.0±5.7) years (range:54 to 66 years), (61.5±5.8) years (range:54 to 67 years) and (61.3±8.1) years (range:52 to 71 years), respectively. Using computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and patient-specific aortic models, preoperative hemodynamic indices were quantitatively analyzed, including blood flow velocity, pressure distribution, flow distribution, wall shear stress (WSS) and time-averaged wall shear stress (TAWSS).Hemodynamic analyses revealed a stepwise decreasing trend of false lumen (FL) flow rate across the three groups. The preoperative death MCAD group exhibited a significantly higher FL flow ((62.81±7.59)ml/s (range: 56.29 to 73.78 ml/s)) than the non-preoperative death MCAD group ((24.84±9.25)ml/s (range: 17.23 to 36.84 ml/s)) and the non-preoperative death DCAD group ((11.86±5.62)ml/s (range: 6.72 to 19.84 ml/s)). The intergroup variation patterns of FL flow ratio and maximum FL TAWSS were highly consistent. The preoperative death MCAD group yielded values of 0.77±0.16 (range: 0.56 to 0.93) and (34.44±6.50)Pa (range: 27.54 to 41.38 Pa),which were elevated compared with the non-preoperative death MCAD group (0.44±0.17(range: 0.33 to 0.70), (15.46±7.75)Pa (range: 6.69 to 25.01 Pa)) and the non-preoperative death DCAD group (0.22±0.11(range: 0.14 to 0.37), (20.80±7.34)Pa (range: 15.23 to 31.60 Pa)),whereas no obvious disparities were observed between the latter two groups. In addition,the maximum FL WSS in the preoperative death MCAD group reached (125.76±26.57)Pa (range: 87.55 to 147.91 Pa),markedly exceeding that of the non-preoperative death MCAD group ((64.89±30.45)Pa (range: 28.62 to 102.40 Pa)) and the non-preoperative death DCAD group ((91.15±28.16)Pa (range: 61.51 to 126.41 Pa)).Elevated FL flow and abnormally high shear stress may correlate with poor outcomes in patients with MCAD,and these parameters could serve as potential biomechanical biomarkers. CFD simulation can act as an auxiliary tool to identify high-risk aortic dissection patients,which helps refine clinical management and facilitate individualized precision treatment for MCAD.

Patients with acute uncomplicated Stanford-type B aortic dissection who presented at Zhongshan Hospital, Fudan University between January 2019 and December 2023 were enrolled. Patients were diagnosed as having either double-channeled aortic dissection (DCAD) or MCAD based on preoperative standardized computed-tomography angiography (CTA).

title: [Value of a CT angiography-based deep learning model for differentiating SVS grade Ⅱ and grade Ⅲ blunt thoracic aortic injury: a retrospective multicenter staged study].
abstract: Objectives: Methods: Results: Conclusions: CI To develop a segmentation-guided multitask deep learning model for Society for Vascular Surgery (SVS) grades Ⅰ to Ⅳ classification of blunt thoracic aortic injury (BTAI) and validate its clinical utility for differentiating SVS grades Ⅱ and Ⅲ.This is a retrospective case series study. Computed tomography angiography (CTA) data were collected from 317 patients with BTAI at 12 hospitals in China, including the First Medical Center of Chinese People's Liberation Army General Hospital, West China Hospital of Sichuan University, the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University, the Affiliated Hospital of Southwest Medical University, and other local hospitals, between January 2006 and May 2026. The cohort included 258 male and 59 female patients, with an age of (54.8±15.3) years (range:16 to 92 years). The 253-patient development cohort was divided using a patient-level random split stratified by SVS injury grade and source center at an approximate ratio of 8∶2 into a training set of 202 patients and an internal validation set of 51 patients. The 64 BTAI cases from the Affiliated Hospital of Southwest Medical University were locked in advance as an independent external test set. The model consisted of a shared encoder, a lesion-segmentation branch, and a mask-guided classification branch. The primary outcomes were the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and grade Ⅲ sensitivity for differentiating SVS grade Ⅱ (intramural hematoma) from grade Ⅲ (pseudoaneurysm) in the external test set. Secondary outcomes included segmentation, automated measurements, and offline reader-study results.The internal validation set covered SVS grades Ⅰ to Ⅳ, with an overall grading accuracy of 92.2% (47/51) and a macro-averaged F1 score of 0.919. The external test set included 31 SVS grade Ⅱ (intramural hematoma) cases and 33 SVS grade Ⅲ (pseudoaneurysm) cases. The model had an AUC of 0.968 (95%:0.924 to 0.996), an accuracy of 92.2% (59/64), grade Ⅲ sensitivity of 93.9% (31/33), and grade Ⅱ specificity of 90.3% (28/31); two grade Ⅲ cases were misclassified as grade Ⅱ. The automated segmentation success rate was 96.9% (62/64), the overall lesion Dice similarity coefficient was 0.872±0.072 (range:0.46 to 0.99), and model inference time per case was (15.4±2.4) s (range:10.8 to 22.6 s). In the fixed-sequence reader study, six junior physicians had higher grade Ⅱ/Ⅲ accuracy and grade Ⅲ sensitivity and shorter interpretation times during the artificial intelligence-assisted phase than during the unaided phase.The segmentation-guided CTA deep learning model developed in this study performed BTAI lesion segmentation, SVS grading, and measurement of key morphologic parameters, and maintained good discrimination between SVS grades Ⅱ and Ⅲ in the independent external test set. Model assistance may help reduce missed grade Ⅲ cases by junior physicians and shorten interpretation time, thereby supporting standardized imaging assessment of BTAI.

title: [Is there still a role for manual deployment techniques in the era of fenestrated/branched endovascular aortic repair? Normative boundaries and practical value in the management of hostile aortic landing zones].
abstract: Standard endovascular aortic repair has been widely used for the treatment of abdominal aortic aneurysms and selected complex aortic diseases because of its minimally invasive nature, rapid recovery, and favorable perioperative safety profile. However, in hostile aortic landing zones characterized by a short neck, severe angulation, conical neck configuration, mural thrombus, or circumferential calcification, standard endovascular repair remains associated with inadequate proximal apposition, type Ⅰ endoleak, endograft migration, and secondary intervention. Manual deployment techniques, including the push-up technique, reverse slider technique, Kabedon technique, and stepwise controlled deployment, may improve endograft axial alignment, proximal edge positioning, and local wall apposition to some extent; however, their role is mainly limited to optimization of the deployment process and cannot replace the principle of a durable sealing zone. This review summarizes the anatomical characteristics of hostile aortic landing zones, the mechanisms and clinical evidence of manual deployment techniques, the standardized value of fenestrated/branched endovascular aortic repair and physician-modified endografts, adjunctive fixation and intraoperative bailout techniques, and application scenarios in emergency repair of ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysms. The aim is to provide a practical reference for rational selection between optimized deployment of standard endografts and complex sealing-zone reconstruction in complex endovascular aortic repair.

title: [Technical considerations and advances in distal bypass for chronic limb-threatening ischemia of the lower extremities].
abstract: Chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) represents the end stage of lower extremity arterial disease and is associated with high rates of disability and mortality. With the rapid advancement of endovascular techniques, an "endovascular-first" strategy has become widely adopted. However, for patients with complex, long-segment, heavily calcified, diffuse, inflammatory lesions, or those with repeated endovascular failure, distal bypass surgery remains an indispensable option for limb salvage. The success of distal bypass depends not only on advanced surgical expertise but also on appropriate patient selection, accurate assessment of inflow and outflow tracts, optimal conduit choice, and meticulous perioperative management. Based on recent international guidelines and clinical evidence, this review focuses on key technical aspects of distal bypass, including inflow selection, target artery assessment, conduit selection, graft tunneling, distal anastomosis, intraoperative flow assessment, postoperative antithrombotic therapy and wound management. It also discusses the appropriate role of these techniques in the comprehensive treatment of CLTI based on recent evidence-based medical findings. In addition, emerging developments such as alternative conduits, and gene/cell therapy are discussed, aiming to provide insights into optimizing revascularization strategies for patients with CLTI.

title: [From critical evaluation based on the gold standard to precision full-process management: advances in the diagnosis and treatment framework for aortic arch artery pathologies].
abstract: Supra-aortic arch artery diseases, including lesions of the carotid,subclavian,and vertebral arteries,represent major causes of cerebral and upper extremity ischemia. The diagnostic and therapeutic strategies for these conditions are undergoing a profound transformation-from conventional open surgery toward minimally invasive endovascular treatment,and further to individualized precision medicine. Recent advances in imaging assessment have substantially improved lesion characterization and risk stratification. The iterative evolution of endovascular devices has enhanced procedural safety. Meanwhile,several topics have become research hotspots,the evidence-based comparison between transcarotid artery revascularization and transfemoral carotid stenting;the renewed pathophysiological understanding of subclavian steal syndrome and vertebral artery diseases;and the construction of individualized treatment decision-making frameworks. Nevertheless,current clinical practice still faces challenges such as controversies over optimal surgical approaches,insufficient prevention and management of complications,and a lack of robust long-term outcome data. From the perspective of vascular surgery,this article systematically reviews recent advances in endovascular devices,surgical techniques,and treatment concepts,aiming to provide front-line clinicians with up-to-date,practical,and actionable insights into the management of supra-aortic arch artery diseases.

title: [A brief discussion on the progress and development directions of clinical research in vascular surgery].
abstract: Vascular surgery has experienced rapid development over the past three decades. With the application of minimally invasive and interventional techniques in the diagnosis and treatment of vascular diseases, clinical research and technological innovation in vascular surgery have expanded significantly. As populations aging accelerates globally-including in China-and the number of patients with cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease within the existing healthcare system becomes increasingly evident. The future of vascular surgery will center on three core principles: minimization, precision, and intelligence. By integrating breakthroughs in basic science, engineering, and artificial intelligence, clinical translation will be accelerated. The discipline will shift from "disease treatment" to "health management", and from a "surgery-centered" single model to a "patient-centered" integrated approach model. Future developments will further incorporate artificial intelligence, big data models, precision medicine, more advanced and comprehensive minimally invasive technologies, enhancing multidisciplinary collaboration and preventive care. These advancements are expected to significantly improve diagnostic accuracy, treatment outcomes, and quality of life for patients with vascular diseases.

title: Association of muscle strength with the incidence of venous thromboembolism and all-cause mortality among patients: a prospective cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Muscle strength is a well-established indicator of overall health, yet its prospective association with the incidence and prognosis of venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains inconsistent. METHODS: This prospective cohort study included 481 945 participants without prior VTE from the UK Biobank for incidence analysis, and 14 908 patients with prevalent VTE at baseline for prognostic analysis. Muscle strength was assessed using grip strength relative to body weight and categorised into sex- and age-specific tertiles. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for incident VTE and all-cause mortality. RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 13.72 years, 15 774 incident VTE events were documented. Each 1-standard deviation increase in muscle strength was associated with a 13% reduction in VTE risk (HR 0.87, 95% CI: 0.85-0.89). Compared with the low muscle strength group, participants in the middle and high tertiles had 12% (HR 0.88, 95% CI: 0.84-0.92) and 19% (HR 0.81, 95% CI: 0.77-0.84) lower risk of VTE. This inverse association remained consistent across all genetic risk strata. Among patients with VTE, 2884 deaths occurred during follow-up. Each 1-standard deviation increase was associated with a 14% lower mortality risk (HR 0.86, 95% CI: 0.82-0.90). High and middle muscle strength were associated with 21% (HR 0.79, 95% CI: 0.72-0.87) and 17% (HR 0.83, 95% CI: 0.76-0.91) lower all-cause mortality versus low strength. CONCLUSION: Higher muscle strength is associated with a lower risk of incident VTE, regardless of genetic predisposition, and with lower mortality among patients with VTE.

title: Precision medicine meets vascular disease: innovations in atherosclerotic renal artery stenosis management.
abstract: Atherosclerotic renal artery stenosis (ARAS) is a significant cause of secondary hypertension and kidney injury with important cardiovascular consequences. This review briefly discusses the pathophysiology of ARAS, evaluates in-depth the diagnostic performance of duplex ultrasound, computed tomography angiography, and magnetic resonance angiography, and synthesizes results from major randomized trials and observational studies to explore current treatment options. The objective is to define the current diagnostic and therapeutic landscape of ARAS in a manner that supports evidence-based clinical decision making, and identify which treatment modality may be appropriate based on clinical presentation. The preference for optimized medical therapy as the initial standard of care is largely based on multiple randomized controlled trials (RCTs), which found no overall benefit from invasive endovascular treatments in conjunction with medical therapy. However, the limitations in trial design indicate that these results do not rule out the benefit in carefully selected patients. Evidence from subgroup analyses and non-randomized studies supports invasive endovascular revascularization in presentations such as recurrent flash pulmonary edema, progressive decline in renal function, and hypertension resistant to pharmacologic medical therapy. Endovascular stenting is preferred when anatomy is favorable, while open surgical reconstruction, including aortorenal bypass or endarterectomy, is reserved for complex lesions, failed prior endovascular intervention, or concomitant aortic surgery. The review also discusses emerging strategies, including novel stent platforms and drug-eluting technology, which may improve outcomes if validated in targeted high-risk cohorts.

title: Major re-amputation after initial diabetic foot amputation: A retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Reamputation after initial diabetic foot amputation remains a major clinical challenge associated with substantial morbidity. Identifying factors related to major reamputation may improve patient management and limb preservation. This study evaluated the impact of clinical, metabolic, nutritional, and vascular parameters on the risk of major reamputation. This retrospective cohort study included 141 patients who underwent lower-extremity amputation for diabetic foot disease between 2020 and 2025. Demographic variables, body mass index (BMI), smoking status, peripheral arterial disease (PAD), infection history, glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) levels, and Prognostic Nutritional Index (PNI) were analyzed. Major reamputation was defined as a subsequent ipsilateral amputation progressing to a below-knee or above-knee level; contralateral amputations and more proximal minor amputations confined to the foot were not considered outcome events. The median follow-up was 3.0 years (range, 1-5). Continuous variables were compared using the Mann-Whitney U test and categorical variables using the Pearson chi-square test. Kaplan-Meier analysis was used to estimate major reamputation-free survival, and Cox proportional hazards regression was performed to evaluate factors associated with time to major reamputation. A Fine-Gray competing-risk analysis was additionally performed considering death before major reamputation as a competing event. Major reamputation occurred in 31 patients (22.0%). Patients with reamputation had significantly lower BMI and PNI values and higher HbA1c levels (all P < .001). Smoking and PAD were significantly more frequent in the reamputation group (both P < .001), whereas no significant between-group differences were observed for age, sex, serum albumin, or infection history. In multivariable Cox regression analysis, PAD (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 6.25, 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.13-18.32, P < .001) and higher HbA1c (adjusted HR 1.40, 95% CI 1.19-1.65, P < .001) were independently associated with an increased hazard of major reamputation, whereas higher PNI was associated with a reduced hazard (adjusted HR 0.95, 95% CI 0.91-0.99, P = .009). Lower BMI, higher HbA1c, reduced PNI, smoking, and PAD were associated with major reamputation. In multivariable time-to-event analysis, PAD, HbA1c, and PNI remained independently associated with the outcome. These findings demonstrate associations between routinely available clinical parameters and major reamputation and warrant further evaluation in prospective studies.

Identifying factors related to major reamputation may improve patient management and limb preservation. This study evaluated the impact of clinical, metabolic, nutritional, and vascular parameters on the risk of major reamputation.

title: Development and internal validation of machine-learning models for postoperative deep vein thrombosis after hip arthroplasty for femoral neck fracture: evaluation of Traditional Chinese Medicine syndrome features.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Postoperative lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT) remains a clinically important complication after hip arthroplasty for femoral neck fracture. We evaluated whether Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) syndrome features add predictive information beyond conventional preoperative variables and examined the association between the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index and postoperative DVT. METHODS: n n This retrospective single-center study included 380 patients. Group-constrained partitioning and resampling prevented identical prespecified multivariable profiles from crossing evaluation boundaries, yielding a development set ( = 267; 74 DVT events) and a profile-disjoint held-out validation set ( = 113; 31 events). Nine machine-learning algorithms were evaluated using a fixed eight-variable panel comprising D-dimer, fibrinogen, platelet count, type 2 diabetes, fasting blood glucose, TyG, Qi stagnation with blood stasis (QSBS), and Qi deficiency with blood stasis (QDBS). Random forest (RF) was selected on the basis of development-set out-of-fold performance before held-out validation. RESULTS: p p p p Postoperative DVT occurred in 105 patients (27.6%). RF achieved a pooled group-aware development out-of-fold AUC of 0.774 (95% CI 0.710-0.837) and a held-out validation AUC of 0.859 (95% CI 0.782-0.935). Across 30 repeated group-constrained partitions, mean validation AUC was 0.792. In the single profile-disjoint held-out validation partition, the development-derived threshold of 0.298 yielded sensitivity of 0.903, specificity of 0.720, positive predictive value of 0.549, and negative predictive value of 0.952; in that same partition, the calibration slope was 1.136 (95% CI 0.753-1.867), the observed-to-expected ratio was 0.846, and the Brier score was 0.132. Adding QSBS and QDBS did not materially improve discrimination (AUC 0.855 vs. 0.859; ΔAUC = 0.003; DeLong = 0.746). Higher TyG remained associated with DVT after multivariable adjustment (OR per 1 SD 1.550, 95% CI 1.186-2.026; = 0.001); restricted cubic splines supported an overall association ( = 0.007) without significant evidence of nonlinearity ( = 0.082). CONCLUSION: RF showed favorable discrimination in the held-out cohort but more modest performance across repeated group-constrained partitions. The two retained TCM syndrome variables did not provide a material increment in AUC, whereas higher TyG remained associated with postoperative DVT after multivariable adjustment. External validation and assessment of recalibration are required before clinical implementation.

title: Serial computed tomography angiography-based computational fluid dynamics characterizes reduced near-renal tear exchange in kidneys that develop atrophy after aortic dissection repair.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Renal atrophy may develop after aortic dissection repair despite an anatomically patent renal artery on computed tomography angiography (CTA). This exploratory study compared serial near-renal aortic hemodynamics between kidneys with and without later renal-volume loss. METHODS: Six index kidneys from six men were studied: three with ≥30% loss of reference volume (atrophy group) and three age-matched comparators. Patient-specific computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models were built from preoperative, early postoperative and late follow-up CTA; within each patient, inlet and outlet (three-element Windkessel) boundary conditions were identical across time points. All 90 true-lumen/false-lumen (TL/FL) communications were characterized by distance from the renal-ostial plane, direction, pressure difference and trans-tear flow. TL/FL relationships were quantified at the renal-ostial plane, and bilateral renal-artery flow was computed directly. Renal volume was measured by three-dimensional CTA segmentation. RESULTS: versus versus versus versus All six index kidneys were supplied from the FL before repair. Index-kidney volume changed by -53.0%, -64.1% and -50.6% in the atrophy group and by -13.8%, +0.8% and -10.7% in comparators. No hemodynamic measure separated the groups before repair. From the early postoperative model onward (3-37 days), two aortic-level flow measures were lower in every atrophy kidney than in every comparator: the FL flow-magnitude fraction at the renal-ostial plane (0.03-0.100.13-0.79) and total peak-systolic trans-communication flow (37.8-45.161.8-185.3 mL/s). Index renal-artery flow separated the groups only at late follow-up (-29.4%, -32.6% and -63.9%+5.9%, -7.4% and -3.0%), as did tear-exchange flow directed toward the renal-ostial level (1.9-19.138.7-130.9 mL/s). FL/TL pressure ratios did not separate the groups at any time point. In one patient-derived geometry, sequential virtual closure of idealized communications redistributed and reversed flow in the remaining communications; index renal-artery flow after the final closure was similar to baseline. CONCLUSION: In kidneys that later atrophied, the FL flow contribution at the renal level was lower than in comparators early after repair, before the modeled decrease in renal-artery flow and, in two of three kidneys, before substantial volume loss. Given three kidneys per group and multiple measures, these associations are hypothesis-generating and do not establish causation, renal parenchymal perfusion or a treatment threshold.

This exploratory study compared serial near-renal aortic hemodynamics between kidneys with and without later renal-volume loss. METHODS: Six index kidneys from six men were studied: three with ≥30% loss of reference volume (atrophy group) and three age-matched comparators.

title: Prognostic performance of the WIfI classification in diabetic patients with infrapopliteal CLTI after endovascular revascularization: a subgroup analysis of the PRIME-WIFI registry.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: The Wound, Ischemia, and foot Infection (WIfI) classification is widely used in chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI). However, its prognostic performance in diabetic patients after endovascular revascularization remains unclear. We evaluated its prognostic and discriminatory performance in this population. METHODS: This subgroup analysis of the prospective, multicenter PRIME-WIFI registry included diabetic patients with infrapopliteal CLTI undergoing endovascular revascularization. Associations between baseline WIfI stage and MAE (all-cause mortality, major amputation, or clinically driven target-limb reintervention), its individual components, amputation-free survival, clinical improvement, and 12-month VascuQoL change were assessed using Kaplan-Meier, multivariable Cox, and Harrell's C-index analyses. RESULTS: P n P P P P P P P P P P P P A total of 707 diabetic patients (730 limbs) were analyzed; in the full PRIME-WIFI cohort, diabetes status showed a borderline interaction with WIfI stage for MAE (for interactio = 0.083). One-year freedom from MAE decreased across WIfI stages (89.5%, 77.4%, 78.0%, and 70.1% for stages 1-4; log-rank = 0.004), and WIfI stage independently predicted MAE (HR: 1.31; 95% CI: 1.09-1.56; = 0.0031). One-year AFS was 94.7%, 83.3%, 83.3%, and 74.2% (log-rank = 0.0003), with higher WIfI stage associated with worse AFS (HR: 1.53; 95% CI: 1.24-1.89; < 0.001). Overall survival was 94.7%, 87.8%, 86.1%, and 80.3% (log-rank = 0.009), and WIfI stage was independently associated with mortality (HR: 1.52; 95% CI: 1.20-1.94; < 0.001). Freedom from major amputation was 100.0%, 95.3%, 96.8%, and 92.3% (log-rank = 0.02), with higher WIfI stage independently associated with major amputation (HR: 1.62; 95% CI: 1.07-2.57; = 0.020). In contrast, freedom from CD-TLR did not differ significantly across stages (log-rank = 0.60; HR: 0.92; 95% CI: 0.68-1.23; = 0.564). Clinical improvement tended to decrease with increasing WIfI stage but did not reach statistical significance ( = 0.053). VascuQoL scores improved from baseline to 12 months across all WIfI stages, with no significant difference in the magnitude of improvement among stages (time-by-WIfI interaction = 0.247). CONCLUSIONS: In this diabetic subgroup, WIfI retained prognostic value for MAE, AFS, mortality, and major amputation. However, discrimination was clearest between stages 1 and 4, with limited separation between stages 2 and 3. These findings support WIfI for broad risk stratification while highlighting the need for complementary assessment in diabetic CLTI.

However, its prognostic performance in diabetic patients after endovascular revascularization remains unclear. We evaluated its prognostic and discriminatory performance in this population.

title: Prognostic Value of the Frailty Index in Patients with Severe Aortic Regurgitation Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Frailty represents a multidimensional vulnerability that predicts poor outcomes in cardiovascular disease. Its prognostic value in patients with severe native aortic regurgitation (AR) undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is not well defined. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether an abbreviated cumulative deficit frailty index predicts one-year all-cause mortality and to explore its interaction with N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide in this population. METHODS: In this post hoc analysis of the prospective China DVD2 multicenter cohort, 298 patients with isolated severe AR who underwent TAVR were included. Frailty was assessed preprocedurally using an abbreviated 8-9-item cumulative deficit frailty index (FI) encompassing functional, cognitive, nutritional, and clinical domains. The primary endpoint was one-year all-cause mortality. The cohort-derived FI threshold for mortality was derived using time-dependent receiver operating characteristic analysis. Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, atrial fibrillation, and NT-proBNP were applied. Subgroup and interaction analyses were performed. RESULTS: The cohort-derived FI threshold was 0.407, classifying 32 patients as high frailty. High-FI patients exhibited greater symptom burden, higher prevalence of atrial fibrillation, larger left atrial diameter, and elevated NT-proBNP. One-year mortality was significantly higher in the high-FI group compared with low-FI patients (15.6% vs 3.4%, P = 0.010). High FI was associated with higher one-year mortality in Model 3 (HR 4.00, 95% CI 1.18-13.50; P = 0.026). No significant multiplicative or additive interaction with NT-proBNP was observed. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients undergoing TAVR for severe native aortic regurgitation, a high FI was associated with higher one-year mortality. These findings extend prior evidence on the prognostic implications of frailty to this understudied population.

title: Development of a multidisciplinary service-delivery framework for venous thromboembolism prevention in hospitalized medical patients with lung cancer: a mixed-methods modified Delphi study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a common and potentially preventable complication in patients with lung cancer. Although clinical guidelines recommend risk assessment and appropriate prophylaxis, hospitals often lack operational frameworks for translating these recommendations into multidisciplinary workflows, quality monitoring, and continuous improvement. This study aimed to develop a hospital-based multidisciplinary service-delivery framework for VTE prevention and management among hospitalized medical patients with lung cancer. METHODS: A mixed-methods modified Delphi study was conducted. Candidate framework items were generated from a structured literature review and semi-structured interviews with physicians, nurses, clinical pharmacists, and hospital managers, and were organized using Donabedian's Structure-Process-Outcome model. A two-round Delphi survey was then conducted with 15 experts from respiratory medicine, oncology, clinical pharmacy, nursing management, and hospital quality management. Experts rated the importance and feasibility of each candidate item, and the framework was refined using predefined consensus criteria and qualitative feedback. RESULTS: The response rate was 100% in both Delphi rounds. Expert authority coefficients were 0.943 and 0.953 in rounds 1 and 2, respectively. Kendall's W ranged from 0.249 to 0.292, indicating low-to-moderate concordance despite statistically significant tests. The final framework included 3 first-level domains, 11 second-level components, and 34 third-level indicators covering structural capacity, care processes, and outcome monitoring. Importance ratings were generally higher than feasibility ratings, particularly for indicators requiring information system support, multidisciplinary coordination, and post-discharge continuity of care. CONCLUSION: This study developed a preliminary, consensus-based multidisciplinary service-delivery framework for hospital-based VTE prevention in patients with lung cancer. The framework may support the operationalization of guideline recommendations, standardization of care processes, and prioritization of quality improvement efforts. Prospective implementation studies are needed to evaluate its feasibility, transferability, and impact on care quality and patient outcomes.

title: Emergent or urgent hybrid repair for complex thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms: single-centre experience.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Emergent or urgent repair of thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms (TAAA) always represent a major challenge due to high mortality and complex reconstruction of visceral arteries. We aimed to evaluate the short- and long-term outcomes of patients undergoing emergent or urgent hybrid TAAA repair under a standardized institutional perioperative protocol. METHODS: This study represents a retrospective cohort analysis of data derived from a prospectively maintained institutional database at West China Hospital. All consecutive patients who underwent emergent or urgent hybrid repair for TAAA between January 2013 and February 2025 were included. RESULTS: n n n n The cohort comprised 38 TAAA patients (31 male, with a median age of 50.5 years) who underwent emergent/urgent hybrid repair. The median aneurysm length was 200.9 mm (IQR 154.0-320.0), with a mean maximum diameter was 70.5 ± 17.8 mm. Intraoperatively, 4 visceral arteries (IQR 4-5) were reconstructed. Median operative time was 415 min (IQR 360-504), with median ICU and postoperative hospital stays of 96.0 h (IQR 46.5-203.5) and 17 days (IQR 11-24), respectively. No myocardial infarction or hepatic failure occurred. Postoperative complications included pulmonary infection ( = 4, 10.5%), acute kidney injury ( = 2, 5.3%), and spinal cord ischemia ( = 5, 13.2%). Thirty-day mortality was 10.5% ( = 4). The survival rates at 12 and 60 months postoperatively were 86.8% (95% CI 76.7-98.3) and 83.0% (95% CI 71.7-96.6). The free of reintervention rates at 12 and 60 months postoperatively were 90.5% (95% CI 80.8-100.0) and 76.4% (95% CI 61.1-95.7). CONCLUSION: In this selected cohort managed with a standardized perioperative protocol, emergent and urgent hybrid TAAA repair was feasible, with acceptable perioperative mortality and durable mid- to long-term survival. However, the occurrence of spinal cord ischemia represents a substantial and clinically significant trade-off of this approach in the emergency setting. Moreover, these favorable survival outcomes should be interpreted in the context of the cohort's relatively young age and favorable baseline risk profile. These findings emphasize that survival benefit is counterbalanced by significant neurological morbidity, highlighting the need for refined spinal protection protocols in urgent cases and for comparative studies to validate the specific efficacy of this standardized protocol.

We aimed to evaluate the short- and long-term outcomes of patients undergoing emergent or urgent hybrid TAAA repair under a standardized institutional perioperative protocol. METHODS: This study represents a retrospective cohort analysis of data derived from a prospectively maintained institutional database at West China Hospital.

title: Personalised approach to venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in heavier critically ill patients (PROSPER): A randomised, parallel-group, electronic medical record (EMR)-embedded feasibility trial.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Data are limited regarding optimal low molecular weight heparin dosing for venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in heavier critically ill patients. This trial evaluated the feasibility of a weight-based dynamic dosing algorithm. DESIGN SETTING PARTICIPANTS: Open-label, electronic medical record-embedded randomised feasibility trial. Patients, weighing ≥100 kg who required thromboprophylaxis were eligible. Enoxaparin was commenced with weight-based dosing and anti-Xa level-guided adjustment (target peak anti-Xa level 0.2-0.4 IU/mL) or usual care (40 mg twice daily). MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary outcome was peak anti-Xa level at 'steady state' (after ≥3 enoxaparin doses). The feasibility threshold was set at 95% of steady state anti-Xa levels in the intervention group being less than the threshold for therapeutic anticoagulant effect (≤0.6 IU/mL). RESULTS: Fifty participants (intervention n = 17, control n = 33) received 331 doses of enoxaparin (median of 4 [interquartile range {IQR}: 3-7] doses per participant, and a dose of 50 [IQR: 50-60] mg (intervention) and 40 [IQR: 40-40] mg (control)). Thirty-two 'steady state' peak anti-Xa measurements were recorded from 24 patients (12 intervention and 12 control). The proportion of peak anti-Xa levels that were ≤0.6 IU/mL was: 15 of 17 (88%) vs. 15 of 15 (100%). There were fewer peak anti-Xa measurements below the prophylactic range (<0.2 IU/mL) in the intervention group compared with the control group (2 of 17 [12%] vs. 5 of 15 [33%]). Six patients developed venous thrombosis or pulmonary embolism (2 of 17 [12%] vs. 4 of 33 [12%]). Major bleeding occurred in one patient in the intervention group. CONCLUSIONS: A weight-based dynamic thromboprophylaxis algorithm was implemented via the electronic medical record but did not meet the predefined feasibility threshold.

This trial evaluated the feasibility of a weight-based dynamic dosing algorithm. DESIGN SETTING PARTICIPANTS: Open-label, electronic medical record-embedded randomised feasibility trial.

title: Multimodal integration of carotid plaque ultrasound radiomics and dynamic systemic immune-inflammation trajectories for subacute risk stratification after stroke thrombectomy: development and internal validation of an exploratory prognostic model.
abstract: BACKGROUND: We hypothesized that integrating macroscopic carotid plaque architecture, quantified via ultrasound radiomics, with downstream micro-cellular temporal dynamics, defined by longitudinal immune trajectories, would yield a highly accurate prognostic framework for 90-day functional outcomes in patients undergoing endovascular thrombectomy (EVT). METHODS: N N This single-center, retrospective cohort study consecutively included 316 AIS-LVO patients who underwent successful EVT (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction score ≥2b) within 24 h of symptom onset. Patients were partitioned into a discovery ( = 221) and an internal validation cohort ( = 95) using stratified random sampling. To capture temporal inflammatory heterogeneity, the Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index (SII) was measured at days 0, 1, 3, and 7, and clustered using Latent Class Mixed Models (LCMM). Concurrently, high-dimensional radiomic features strictly adhering to the Image Biomarker Standardisation Initiative (IBSI) guidelines were extracted from baseline two-dimensional carotid ultrasound images. A radiomics score (Rad-score) was constructed utilizing Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regression. Four progressive predictive models were developed, culminating in an Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) multimodal architecture. The primary endpoint was an unfavorable 90-day functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale score 3 to 6). RESULTS: p p p An unfavorable outcome occurred in 166 of 316 patients (52.5%). The LCMM objectively identified three longitudinal SII phenotypes. The "persistent high-inflammation" trajectory (Class 3, 17.0% of patients) was independently associated with an increased risk of an unfavorable outcome compared to the "rapid resolution" trajectory (Class 1) [adjusted odds ratio (aOR), 4.85; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.20 to 10.85; < 0.001]. The ultrasound Rad-score, comprising 9 core textural features, also demonstrated robust independent predictive value (aOR, 1.52; 95% CI, 1.21 to 1.92 per 0.1-point increase; < 0.001). In the strictly isolated internal validation cohort, the full multimodal XGBoost model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.92 (95% CI, 0.86 to 0.97), with an accuracy of 86.3%, sensitivity of 88.0%, and specificity of 84.4%. This performance was statistically superior to the standard clinical baseline model (AUC, 0.74; 95% CI, 0.63 to 0.84; < 0.001 via DeLong test). Furthermore, the multimodal paradigm demonstrated clinical reclassification utility, yielding a continuous net reclassification improvement of 0.985 (95% CI, 0.684 to 1.286) and an integrated discrimination improvement of 0.194 (95% CI, 0.128 to 0.260). CONCLUSION: An exploratory model integrating baseline carotid plaque ultrasound radiomics with Day-0-to-Day-7 systemic immune-inflammation trajectories was associated with 90-day functional outcome after EVT and, on internal validation, discriminated outcomes more strongly than a conventional clinical model. Because the immune-trajectory component is only complete at Day 7, the model is intended for subacute post-EVT risk stratification rather than acute treatment selection, and requires external, prospective validation before any clinical application.

title: Inflammation-associated clinical prognostic factors and primary patency after drug-coated balloon angioplasty for recurrent autogenous arteriovenous fistula stenosis: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Recurrent autogenous arteriovenous fistula (AVF) stenosis occurs in a vascular environment in which injury, neointimal hyperplasia and inflammation may coexist. Whether routine inflammatory or hematological markers contribute to clinical prognosis after drug-coated balloon (DCB) angioplasty remains uncertain. This retrospective study examines clinical outcomes and inflammation-related prognostic associations without assuming that inflammatory pathways were measured or causally established. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort comprised 357 patients treated between February 2023 and May 2026. The primary outcome was time from index DCB angioplasty to clinically driven target-lesion reintervention. Kaplan-Meier and Cox analyses used available follow-up; a separate clinical logistic model addressed failure within 12 months in 356 patients with complete model data. No non-DCB comparator or patient-level molecular measurements were available. RESULTS: 12 Mean brachial-artery flow increased from 288.98 ± 139.37 to 980.92 ± 174.66 mL/min and minimal luminal diameter from 1.52 ± 0.50 to 5.21 ± 0.63 mm (both P < 0.001). Kaplan-Meier primary patency was 95.24%, 84.03%, 68.90%, and 55.40% at 3, 6, 9, and 12 months. In the extended Cox model (338 patients; 191 events), previous PTA count (HR 1.129 per procedure, P = 0.003) and lesion length (HR 1.105 per cm, P = 0.001) were associated with greater hazard; postprocedural flow (HR 0.889 per 100 mL/min, P = 0.014) and red-blood-cell count (HR 0.804 per 10/L, P = 0.027) were associated with lower hazard. The five-fold cross-validated AUC of the clinical 12-month model was 0.706. CONCLUSION: In this selected single-center cohort, recurrent AVF stenosis after DCB angioplasty was associated with previous PTA burden, lesion length, postprocedural flow, and red-blood-cell count. Routine blood-cell measures provide an exploratory inflammation-related clinical context but do not establish inflammatory mechanisms or validate a specific inflammatory biomarker. Independent validation and patient-level inflammatory measurements are required.

title: Outcomes of Single-Branched TEVAR with Cervical Debranching for Zone 0 and Zone 1 Aortic Arch Repair: A VQI Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Single-branched thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) combined with cervical debranching has emerged as a less invasive alternative to open aortic arch reconstruction for patients requiring zone 0 or zone 1 proximal seal. Contemporary multicenter outcomes of this hybrid approach remain poorly defined. We evaluated procedural characteristics and perioperative outcomes of zone 0 and zone 1 single-branched arch TEVAR with cervical debranching using the Society for Vascular Surgery Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI). METHODS: The VQI TEVAR registry was queried to identify patients undergoing single-branched arch TEVAR with cervical debranching. Patients were included if the proximal landing zone was 0 or 1 and distal disease was confined to zone 5 or more proximal. Chimney, fenestration, stented fenestration, custom-manufactured, and physician-modified repairs were excluded. The zone 0 cohort included patients undergoing innominate side-arm branch repair with left common carotid artery (LCCA) and left subclavian artery (LSA) bypass/transposition, whereas the zone 1 cohort included patients undergoing LCCA side-arm branch repair with LSA bypass/transposition. Outcomes were analyzed descriptively. RESULTS: Among 38,215 TEVAR procedures screened, 50 patients met study criteria, including 39 zone 0 and 11 zone 1 repairs. The mean age was 73.8 ± 8.5 years for zone 0 and 71.7 ± 12.3 years for zone 1 patients. Prior aortic surgery was common (61.5% vs. 45.5%). Aneurysm was the most frequent indication for repair (66.7% vs. 72.7%). Staged treatment was performed in 74.4% of zone 0 and 45.5% of zone 1 procedures. The median procedure time was 166 and 163 minutes, respectively. Technical success was achieved in all patients. with no conversions to open repair and no completion type Ia or Ib endoleaks. Cerebrovascular events occurred in 2.6% of zone 0 and 18.2% of zone 1 patients, including stroke in 2.6% and 9.1%, respectively. Spinal cord ischemia occurred in one zone 0 patient (2.6%). Myocardial infarction and postoperative dialysis occurred in 10.3% and 5.1% of zone 0 patients, respectively, and in no zone 1 patients. Thirty-day mortality was 10.3% following zone 0 repair and 0% following zone 1 repair. CONCLUSION: Single-branched arch TEVAR with cervical debranching was feasible in selected VQI patients undergoing zone 0 and zone 1 arch repair. Given the small sample size and limited event counts, these findings should be interpreted as descriptive early outcomes rather than evidence of comparative safety or superiority. Cerebrovascular complications remain an important concern after arch endovascular intervention.

Contemporary multicenter outcomes of this hybrid approach remain poorly defined. We evaluated procedural characteristics and perioperative outcomes of zone 0 and zone 1 single-branched arch TEVAR with cervical debranching using the Society for Vascular Surgery Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI).

title: Tumor necrosis factor inhibitors and cardiovascular outcomes in adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis is associated with persistent systemic inflammation and increased cardiovascular risk. OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between anti-TNF therapy and clinical cardiovascular outcomes in adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis. METHODS: The authors conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis in accordance with PRISMA 2020 and prospectively registered the protocol in PROSPERO (CRD420251270784). Randomized controlled trials and comparative observational studies evaluating anti-TNF therapy versus placebo, no anti-TNF exposure, topical therapy and/or phototherapy, or non-biologic systemic therapy were eligible. Outcomes of interest were Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (MACE), myocardial infarction, stroke, cardiovascular death, heart failure, atrial fibrillation, venous thromboembolism, and all-cause mortality. RESULTS: Fourteen studies were included. In randomized evidence, anti-TNF therapy was not associated with significant differences in the risk of MACE, myocardial infarction, stroke, or heart failure. In observational analyses stratified by comparator, anti-TNF therapy was associated with a lower pooled risk of reported cardiovascular events versus topical therapy, but not versus oral therapy or phototherapy. STUDY LIMITATIONS: The available evidence was limited by short follow-up in randomized trials, low cardiovascular event counts, wide confidence intervals, and indirect assessment of cardiovascular outcomes, as most trials were designed primarily for dermatologic efficacy and general safety rather than cardiovascular endpoints. CONCLUSIONS: Anti-TNF agents were not associated with a clear increase in major cardiovascular risk and appear to have an acceptable short-term cardiovascular safety profile. However, current evidence does not establish a conclusive cardioprotective effect, and larger prospective studies with longer follow-up are needed.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between anti-TNF therapy and clinical cardiovascular outcomes in adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis. title: Revascularization of Asymptomatic Carotid Artery Stenosis: Cognitive Results of the CREST-2 Randomized Trials.
abstract: IMPORTANCE: Studies show that asymptomatic carotid artery stenosis is associated with diminished cognition. Whether carotid revascularization leads to cognitive improvement is unclear. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether carotid revascularization improves cognition. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Prespecified cognitive secondary outcomes of the CREST-2 randomized clinical trials of patients 35 years or older with 70% or greater asymptomatic carotid stenosis. Enrollment was December 2014 through July 2024, and follow-up ended July 2025. Five cognitive tests were administered before treatment and annually up to 4 years. Cognitive performances from 146 clinical sites were centrally assessed by telephone, blinded to treatment. INTERVENTIONS: Two trials compared carotid stenting plus intensive medical management (CAS + IMM) with IMM alone and carotid endarterectomy plus IMM (CEA + IMM) with IMM alone. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Five cognitive tests, assessing learning, memory, executive function, attention, and processing speed, administered to all patients, were assessed for unadjusted and adjusted mean z scores using a linear mixed model. The minimal clinically important difference was 0.50 SD between treatment groups. The prespecified primary analysis was the fully adjusted composite z score at 4 years. Secondary analyses assessed the individual tests and at the test intervals. RESULTS: Among 2366 US study patients, 2165 (91.5%) participated in cognitive assessments, 1078 in the CAS trial (529 CAS + IMM; 549 IMM alone) and 1087 in the CEA trial (543 CEA + IMM; 544 IMM alone); mean age was 70.1 years (SD, 7.7) and 37.8% were female. Following baseline, 4954 test batteries were administered for a mean of 2.24 (SD, 1.09) follow-up years. There were no treatment-related differences in the fully adjusted estimated composite z scores at 4 years for either the CAS trial (CAS + IMM, 0.22 [95% CI, 0.13 to 0.30] vs IMM alone, 0.18 [95% CI, 0.09 to 0.27]; between-group difference, 0.03 [95% CI, -0.09 to 0.15]) or the CEA trial (CEA + IMM, 0.25 [95% CI, 0.17 to 0.33] vs IMM, 0.23 [95% CI, 0.15 to 0.32]; between-group difference, 0.02 [95% CI, -0.09 to 0.14]). There were no significant differences between revascularization plus medical management vs IMM alone for any individual cognitive test. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In patients with severe asymptomatic carotid artery stenosis, revascularization with either CAS or CEA plus IMM, compared with IMM alone, did not significantly improve cognitive function at up to 4 years of follow-up.

title: Revascularization in Asymptomatic Carotid Artery Stenosis With Hemodynamic Impairment and Cognitive Outcomes: The CREST-H Substudy of the CREST-2 Randomized Clinical Trial.
abstract: IMPORTANCE: Cerebral hemodynamic impairment in patients with asymptomatic internal carotid artery (ICA) stenosis is associated with reduced cognition. It is uncertain whether revascularization might be an effective treatment for cognitive impairment in these patients. OBJECTIVE: To test whether any cognitive benefit from revascularization of high-grade, asymptomatic ICA stenosis varies based on the degree of baseline cerebral hemodynamic impairment. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This substudy was conducted within a multicenter phase 3 randomized clinical trial. Adults (aged 35-86 years) without dementia with eighth-grade education or higher and unilateral asymptomatic ICA stenosis greater than or equal to 70% were enrolled from January 2018 to July 2024 at 61 sites in North America (last follow-up in July 2025). Of 607 participants screened from 2485 in CREST-2, 392 were enrolled. Magnetic resonance or computed tomographic perfusion imaging tested for baseline hemodynamic impairment defined by delayed time-to-peak (TTP) arrival of intravenous contrast in the hemisphere ipsilateral minus contralateral to the stenotic artery. INTERVENTION: Carotid revascularization (endarterectomy or stenting) plus intensive medical management (IMM) vs IMM alone. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was the difference in composite cognitive z score over 1 year based on 5 cognitive tests. The primary analysis tested for an interaction between treatment group (revascularization vs IMM alone) and degree of baseline hemodynamic impairment among those with reduced baseline cognition (cognitive z score ≤-1.0 SD). RESULTS: Of 392 participants enrolled (mean age, 71 years; 125 [32%] females), 61 were excluded for missing baseline imaging and 40 for missing cognitive examinations or other covariates, leaving 291 with complete data. Fifty-one had reduced cognition at baseline (25 in the revascularization group and 26 in the IMM alone group). TTP ranged from no interhemispheric TTP delay to a more-than-2-second delay. Mean (SD) cognitive z scores were -1.36 (0.51) at baseline and -1.17 (0.47) at 1 year in the revascularization group and -1.34 (0.83) at baseline and -1.01 (0.97) at 1 year in the IMM alone group. The primary analysis showed no difference in cognition by treatment group over 1 year, adjusting for treatment group × hemodynamic status interaction and other covariates (adjusted difference in cognitive z score, -0.15 SD [95% CI, -0.54 to 0.24]). The interaction was not significant (β estimate = 0.018 [95% CI, -0.025 to 0.061]; P = .40). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this substudy of a randomized clinical trial, there was no differential effect of revascularization vs IMM alone on cognition over 1 year by cerebral hemodynamic status among those with baseline reduced cognition, suggesting that revascularization does not improve cognitive dysfunction by restoring flow to the brain in chronic asymptomatic carotid stenosis. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03121209.

It is uncertain whether revascularization might be an effective treatment for cognitive impairment in these patients. OBJECTIVE: To test whether any cognitive benefit from revascularization of high-grade, asymptomatic ICA stenosis varies based on the degree of baseline cerebral hemodynamic impairment.

title: Cause-specific mortality after endovascular treatment for anterior vs. posterior circulation large vessel occlusion: a multicenter cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute ischemic stroke due to large vessel occlusion (AIS-LVO) carries substantial mortality despite endovascular treatment (EVT). Whether causes of death differ between anterior (AVO) and posterior (PVO) circulation occlusions is poorly characterized. We compared cause-specific 90-day mortality between patients with AVO and PVO treated with EVT. METHODS: In this multicenter retrospective cohort, consecutive patients with AIS-LVO who underwent EVT at 111 hospitals in China (ANGEL-ACT registry [Endovascular Treatment Key Technique and Emergency Workflow Improvement of acute ischemic stroke]) were included, and adjudicated causes of death were grouped into prespecified categories. Cause-specific mortality was assessed in the complete analytic cohort using the Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard model, with survivors censored at 90 days and deaths from other causes treated as competing events. Cumulative incidence functions were estimated with the Aalen-Johansen estimator. RESULTS: p p p p p p Among 1,671 eligible patients (1,300 AVO, 371 PVO), 228 deaths (13.6%) occurred within 90 days. All-cause mortality was higher in PVO than AVO (19.4% vs. 12.0%). Cerebral edema-related death was significantly more frequent in PVO than AVO (90-day cumulative incidence 9.16% vs. 4.15%; adjusted subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR] 0.47, 95% CI 0.30-0.73,= 0.001; Gray's test< 0.001). Fatal hemorrhagic transformation was numerically more frequent in AVO but did not reach statistical significance in the complete cohort (3.77% vs. 1.89%; adjusted sHR 1.76, 95% CI 0.78-3.98,= 0.17; Gray's test= 0.076), consistent across all sensitivity analyses. Pneumonia-related (adjusted sHR 0.34, 95% CI 0.17-0.68,= 0.003) and recurrent stroke-related (adjusted sHR 0.29, 95% CI 0.10-0.86,= 0.026) deaths were also more frequent in PVO; the pneumonia association remained significant after Bonferroni correction, whereas the recurrent stroke association did not. CONCLUSION: Fatal complications after EVT differ by occlusion territory. Posterior circulation occlusion is independently associated with a higher risk of death from cerebral edema, pneumonia, and recurrent stroke, although the recurrent stroke association did not survive Bonferroni correction. Hemorrhagic transformation accounted for a larger share of anterior circulation deaths, but this did not correspond to a statistically significant increase in risk in the complete cohort.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Acute ischemic stroke due to large vessel occlusion (AIS-LVO) carries substantial mortality despite endovascular treatment (EVT). Whether causes of death differ between anterior (AVO) and posterior (PVO) circulation occlusions is poorly characterized. We compared cause-specific 90-day mortality between patients with AVO and PVO treated with EVT.
