title: Endoscopic versus open great saphenous vein harvesting for lower extremity arterial bypass: A systematic review, meta-analysis and meta-regression.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To compare postoperative outcomes of patients undergoing lower extremity arterial bypass (LEAB) for peripheral artery disease with endoscopic great saphenous vein harvest (EVH) vs open vein harvest (OVH), and to investigate the impact of publication year on bypass patency. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were systematically searched from inception through January 2025 for comparative studies of EVH vs OVH in LEAB. Individual patient data were reconstructed from Kaplan-Meier curves and analyzed using Cox proportional hazards models. Binary and continuous outcomes were pooled using random-effects models. Meta-regression and subgroup analyses by publication year (≤2015 vs >2015) were performed to explore temporal trends in patency. RESULTS: 2 Thirteen retrospective cohort studies comprising 12,401 patients were included. EVH was associated with higher risk of primary patency loss compared with OVH (hazard ratio [HR], 1.32; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.04-1.68; P = .030) and a borderline longer operative time (mean difference, 58.98 minutes; 95% CI, 0.63-117.32; P = .050; I= 96%), but significantly lower wound complications (risk ratio, 0.68; 95% CI, 0.57-0.80; P < .001). No differences were observed in primary-assisted patency, secondary patency, length of stay, major amputation, limb salvage, or mortality. Subgroup analysis showed that the primary patency disadvantage was driven by studies published up to 2015 (HR, 1.49; P = .010), with no significant difference in studies published after 2015 (HR, 0.97; P = .900), although the interaction test was not significant (P = .100). Meta-regression did not demonstrate an association between publication year and primary patency effect size (P = .890). CONCLUSIONS: EVH significantly reduces wound complications but is associated with lower primary patency and potentially longer operative times compared with OVH, disadvantages that do not translate into differences in secondary patency, limb salvage, major amputation, or mortality. Further prospective studies are needed to define the role of EVH to better inform LEAB operative planning.

Individual patient data were reconstructed from Kaplan-Meier curves and analyzed using Cox proportional hazards models.

title: Clinical outcomes of transperitoneal versus retroperitoneal approaches of open aortic repair for abdominal aortic aneurysm stratified by iliac bifurcation involvement.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Aortic aneurysm with iliac bifurcation involvement (AAAIB) is associated with higher rates of systemic comorbidities and increased complexity of open aortic repair (OAR), resulting in worse outcomes compared with OAR for isolated abdominal aortic aneurysm (IAAA). The Society for Vascular Surgery practice guidelines recommend the retroperitoneal approach (RPA) for OAR in certain patients with abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA). However, there is limited evidence to determine whether the relative advantages and disadvantages of RPA and the transperitoneal approach (TPA) change depending on whether the aneurysm distally involves the iliac bifurcation. This study compared the outcomes of TPA and RPA for AAA, stratified by iliac bifurcation involvement, in a multi-institutional, real-world setting. METHODS: The Society for Vascular Surgery Vascular Quality Initiative database was queried for patients who underwent OAR for AAA from January 2003 to September 2024. Patients were stratified as having AAAIB or IAAA based on whether the aneurysm involved the iliac bifurcation and required a distal anastomosis beyond the common iliac artery bifurcation, or not. Baseline characteristics and clinical outcomes, such as overall 30-day mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE: death, myocardial infarction, and stroke), and 1-year survival, were compared between the TPA and RPA groups in patients with IAAA and AAAIB. Univariable and multivariable analyses and a confirmatory analysis with inverse probability-weighted regression were performed. RESULTS: Of all the reviewed patients, 17,009 were included in the final analysis, of whom 15,218 (89.5%) had IAAA and 1791 (10.5%) had AAAIB. Among patients with IAAA, compared with RPA, TPA was associated with a higher odds of overall 30-day mortality (odds ratios [OR], 1.26; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.05-1.49; P = .011) and of MACE (OR, 1.26; 95% CI, 1.11-1.44; P = .001) and a lower 1-year survival rate (hazard ratio, 1.23; 95% CI, 1.09-1.39; P = .001). Among patients with AAAIB, TPA was associated with a lower odds of lower extremity ischemia (OR, 0.47; 95% CI, 0.25-0.91; P = .024), without significant differences in 30-day mortality (OR, 0.80; 95% CI, 0.42-1.51; P = .485), MACE (OR, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.52-1.42; P = .563), and 1-year survival (hazard ratio, 0.93; 95% CI, 0.59-1.47; P = .768). CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world study, iliac bifurcation involvement in AAA was an effect modifier for the outcomes of different OAR approaches. For patients with IAAA, compared with RPA, TPA was associated with worse 30-day mortality, MACE, and 1-year survival. In contrast, for patients with AAAIB, TPA was associated with a lower odds of lower extremity ischemia, without significant differences in 30-day mortality, MACE, or 1-year survival. This study suggests that RPA may be the procedure of choice for IAAA if it is otherwise feasible. However, TPA may be the procedure of choice for patients with AAAIB who are otherwise anatomically suitable. Larger prospective studies are warranted to validate these findings.

title: Prevalence of Guideline-Recommended Genetic Testing in Patients at Risk for Heritable Thoracic Aortic Disease.
abstract: Heritable thoracic aortic diseases (HTAD) include genetic conditions that increase risk of thoracic aortic aneurysm and dissection. The 2022 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association (ACC/AHA) guidelines recommend genetic testing for at-risk individuals, but real-world uptake remains unclear. We evaluated adherence to testing recommendations and demographic differences across major HTAD risk cohorts. We conducted a retrospective study using the TriNetX Research Network (2005-2025). Three guideline-based cohorts were identified using International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM) codes: (1) thoracic aortic aneurysm/dissection before age 60, (2) family history of thoracic aortic disease, and (3) nonthoracic arterial aneurysms. Genetic testing was defined by ICD-10-CM codes for genetic screening or susceptibility. Testing prevalence was stratified by age, sex, race, and ethnicity, and annual testing incidence (2005-2024) was evaluated. Among 57,935 patients with thoracic aortic aneurysm/dissection before age 60, 1,205 (2.09%) underwent genetic testing. Among 2,811,862 patients with a family history of thoracic aortic disease, 66,699 (2.38%) received testing. Among 347,000 patients with nonthoracic arterial aneurysms, 4,913 (1.42%) underwent testing. Testing was consistently higher in females than males and varied across age groups. Annual testing incidence increased over time but remained <0.6% by 2024. In conclusion, genetic testing for HTAD remains markedly underutilized, with <2.5% of at-risk patients tested despite guideline recommendations, highlighting persistent implementation gaps and the need to improve equitable access to genetic evaluation.

We evaluated adherence to testing recommendations and demographic differences across major HTAD risk cohorts.

title: Preoperative White Matter Lesions and Functional Recovery after Revascularization for Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Restoring ambulation is an important goal of revascularization for chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), but predictors of functional recovery remain limited. We investigated whether preoperative white matter lesion (WML) burden was associated with ambulatory recovery after revascularization. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 196 patients with CLTI, tissue loss, Wound, Ischemia, and foot Infection ischemia grade 2 or 3, and brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) within 3 months before revascularization. Preoperative brain MRI was routinely obtained in patients considered for open surgical revascularization for cerebrovascular risk assessment. Periventricular and deep subcortical white matter hyperintensities were graded using the Fazekas scale; a total score of 3 or greater defined a high-grade WML burden. The primary outcome was the achievement of a Functional Ambulation Category score of 3 or greater within 180 days. Associations were evaluated using multivariable Cox models. RESULTS: High-grade WML burden was present in 120 patients. Six-month ambulatory recovery was lower in the high-grade group than in the low-grade group (63.1% vs 82.4%; P = 0.019). High-grade WML burden was independently associated with slower ambulatory recovery (adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 0.65; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.43-0.96; P = 0.032) and delayed final discharge (adjusted HR, 0.63; 95% CI, 0.43-0.92; P = 0.017), but not with wound healing or wound-free functional limb achievement. CONCLUSION: High-grade WML burden was associated with impaired ambulatory recovery and delayed discharge after CLTI revascularization. When preoperative brain MRI is available, WML assessment may complement limb staging and help anticipate rehabilitation and discharge needs.

title: Canadian Cardiovascular Society/Canadian Society of Cardiovascular Surgery/Canadian Association of Interventional Cardiology Clinical Practice Update on Transcatheter Mitral and Tricuspid Valve Intervention: Patient Evaluation and Management.
abstract: The management of mitral valve (MV) and tricuspid valve (TV) regurgitation has undergone significant transformation during the past decade. This change has been driven by a growing understanding of the adverse clinical consequences of these conditions, particularly their strong association with heart failure progression, reduced quality of life, and increased mortality-and by the emergence of effective transcatheter options for valve intervention. Among these, transcatheter MV edge-to-edge repair and replacement and transcatheter tricuspid edge-to-edge repair and replacement have become important therapeutic tools that provide a less invasive alternative to surgery in appropriately selected patients. In this clinical practice update we aim to provide contemporary, evidence-based guidance for clinicians in the evaluation and management of patients with severe, symptomatic MV or TV regurgitation who might benefit from transcatheter intervention. Key topics include the clinical presentation of these valve lesions, the diagnostic evaluation with emphasis on multimodality imaging and hemodynamics, criteria for patient selection, and current data on procedural and long-term clinical outcomes. A central theme is the role of timely referral and structured assessment to avoid missed opportunities for intervention. Optimal outcomes require active engagement from referring physicians and close collaboration within a multidisciplinary heart team, including cardiologists, cardiac surgeons, imaging specialists, heart failure specialists, and nursing partners-to ensure careful patient selection, procedural planning, and comprehensive post-intervention follow-up. By integrating clinical judgement with guideline-based recommendations and procedural expertise, transcatheter edge-to-edge repair or transcatheter valve replacement can offer substantial symptomatic relief and improved quality of life for selected patients, while minimizing procedural risk and enhancing overall cardiovascular outcomes.

title: Thoracic endovascular aortic repair in hyperacute type B aortic dissection: a mini review.
abstract: Thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) is established as the preferred treatment for many patients with complicated acute type B aortic dissection (TBAD). However, its role during the hyperacute phase (within 24 hours of symptom onset) remains controversial, as the acutely dissected aortic wall may be vulnerable to device-related injury. Nevertheless, hyperacute timing should not be regarded as an absolute contraindication to TEVAR. In patients with rupture, malperfusion, impending aortic rupture, persistent pain, refractory hypertension, or progressive true-lumen collapse, prompt entry-tear coverage can restore perfusion and prevent irreversible organ injury. Similarly, in patients without initial complications, high-risk anatomical features may help identify those who could benefit from early intervention. However, evidence supporting routine TEVAR within the first 24 hours remains limited and is predominantly observational. To ensure safe hyperacute TEVAR, careful assessment of the landing zones, conservative device sizing, avoidance of aggressive balloon molding, preservation of branch-vessel and spinal cord perfusion, and prompt recognition of retrograde type A dissection, stroke, spinal cord ischemia, and stent-graft-induced new entry are required. Ultimately, hyperacute TEVAR may be a reasonable option for selected patients with complicated TBAD, with a potential role in high-risk uncomplicated TBAD. Future prospective randomized trials integrating multimodal imaging and dynamic biomarkers are warranted to establish definitive criteria for timing and candidate selection.

title: Limb Salvage Outcomes Following Endovascular Revascularization for Peripheral Artery Disease in a Southern Indian Population: A Single-Center Retrospective Study.
abstract: Background Peripheral artery disease (PAD), particularly chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), is associated with a high risk of limb loss and significant morbidity. Endovascular therapy (ET) has emerged as a minimally invasive alternative to surgical revascularization, especially in high-risk patients and those with comorbidities. This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of ET in achieving limb salvage in a Southern Indian population. Materials and methods This retrospective observational study was conducted at a tertiary vascular care center and included 142 patients with symptomatic PAD who underwent endovascular intervention between July 2023 and June 2025. Clinical severity and lesion complexity were assessed using the Rutherford classification and the TransAtlantic Inter-Society Consensus II (TASC II) classification, respectively. The primary endpoint was limb salvage at one year, defined as freedom from major amputation. Secondary endpoints included technical success, restenosis, and procedure-related complications. Results The study population was predominantly male (87.3%) with a mean age of 61.11 ± 12.90 years. Most patients (78.1%) presented with CLTI. Technical success was achieved in 87.3% of procedures. At one-year follow-up, limb salvage was achieved in 95.8% of patients, with major amputation occurring in 4.2% and minor amputation in 9.1%. Restenosis was observed in 14.7% of cases. Procedure-related complications were infrequent and mostly minor, with one all-cause death during follow-up. Conclusions ET is a safe and effective modality for limb salvage in PAD patients, particularly in populations with a high prevalence of diabetes and advanced disease at presentation. High limb salvage rates can be achieved even in cohorts predominantly comprising patients with CLTI, supporting an endovascular-first approach in appropriately selected patients.

Endovascular therapy (ET) has emerged as a minimally invasive alternative to surgical revascularization, especially in high-risk patients and those with comorbidities. This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of ET in achieving limb salvage in a Southern Indian population.

title: Outcomes among patients with single-vessel tibial runoff undergoing revascularization for chronic limb-threatening ischemia, and the role of peroneal communicating branch quality.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Data evaluating outcomes among patients with single-vessel tibial runoff are limited. Our aim was to compare outcomes across patients with sole anterior tibial (AT), peroneal, or posterior tibial (PT) runoff following revascularization for chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), and to evaluate whether the quality of peroneal communicating branches (PCBs) affects outcome risk within the peroneal runoff population. METHODS: All patients undergoing first-time revascularization for CLTI were retrospectively reviewed (2005-2022) and stratified by sole runoff vessel (AT, peroneal, and PT). Primary outcomes were wound healing, major amputation, major adverse limb events (MALE), and amputation/death, assessed by Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox regression. A subset analysis stratified single-vessel peroneal runoff patients into a three-tiered, PCB grade: Both branches present with at least one robust (PCB grade 1), a single robust branch (PCB grade 2), or no robust branch (PCB grade 3), and compared each with the single-vessel AT/PT reference group. RESULTS: Overall, 732 patients had single-vessel below-knee runoff: 225 AT, 315 peroneal, and 192 PT. Groups differed significantly in age, sex, and diabetes prevalence. Unadjusted 2-year major amputation rates were significantly higher in the peroneal group [19% vs 9.4% (AT) vs 8.7% (PT); P < .001], as were MALE rates (30% vs 14% vs 26%; P = .01). After adjustment, peroneal runoff was independently associated with higher risk of major amputation [hazard ratio (HR), 1.81; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.04-3.13] and MALE (HR, 1.52; 95% CI, 1.03-2.25) compared with AT/PT runoff. These associations persisted in the endovascular cohort (major amputation: HR, 2.09; 95% CI, 1.06-4.13; MALE: HR, 1.59; 95% CI, 1.08-2.35) but did not reach significance in the bypass cohort, which was limited by low-event rates. When patients with single-vessel peroneal runoff were stratified by PCB grades, unadjusted 1-year major amputation rates followed a clear anatomically-driven pattern [6.9% (AT/PT) vs 5.4% (PCB grade 1) vs 15% (PCB grade 2) vs 32% (PCB grade 3); P < .001]. After adjustment, when compared with AT/PT runoff, patients without any robust branch (PCB grade 3) had significantly higher risk of major amputation (HR, 3.21; 95% CI, 1.76-4.84) and MALE (HR, 2.41; 95% CI, 1.53-3.79), whereas those with two communicating branches with at least one being robust (PCB grade 1) demonstrated higher rates of complete wound healing (HR, 1.69; 95% CI, 1.09-2.62) and no difference in major amputation or MALE. CONCLUSIONS: Peroneal runoff is independently associated with worse limb outcomes following revascularization for CLTI, but this risk may be primarily driven by patients with absent or diminutive communicating branches. Patients with robust branching demonstrate outcomes comparable with AT/PT runoff, underscoring the importance of further evaluation and preoperative assessment of PCB quality - using the proposed PCB grading system - in revascularization planning.

title: Impact of prior antithrombotic therapy on safety and outcomes of endovascular therapy in large-core acute ischemic stroke.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Evidence on whether prior antithrombotic drug (ATD) use affects outcomes after endovascular therapy (EVT) is limited in patients with large-core acute ischemic stroke. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This was a subanalysis of the Recovery by Endovascular Salvage for Cerebral Ultra-acute Embolism-Japan Large Ischemic Core Trial, which assessed the efficacy of EVT in patients with large-vessel occlusion and extensive early ischemic changes. The primary outcome was a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0-3 at 90 days. Secondary outcomes included intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) within 48 hours, symptomatic ICH, 90-day mortality, ordinal mRS shift, and ≥8-point improvement in National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score at 48 hours. Logistic regression models were used to assess treatment effects and interactions between ATD and EVT. RESULTS: interaction interaction A total of 202 patients were included (ATD, n = 70; no ATD, n = 132). There was no significant interaction between use of ATD and the effect of EVT in terms of the primary outcome (p=0.944) or secondary outcomes (p=0.218-0.752). In the EVT cohort, prior ATD use was not associated with the primary outcome (adjusted OR 1.16, 95% CI 0.41-3.23). Results were consistent for antiplatelet drugs (adjusted OR 0.70, 95% CI 0.18-2.71) and anticoagulants (adjusted OR 1.52, 95% CI 0.45-5.20). CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory subanalysis, prior ATD use did not significantly modify the observed treatment effect of EVT in patients with large-core acute ischemic stroke. These findings suggest that prior ATD use alone should not preclude consideration of EVT.

The primary outcome was a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0-3 at 90 days.

title: Achieving an endovascular therapy door-to-device time under 90 minutes in patients with ischemic stroke was associated with 90-day mRS.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The American Heart Association (AHA) has a current goal of performing 50% of endovascular therapy (EVT) procedures with a door-to-device (DTD) time of 90 minutes or less for direct arriving patients. Initiatives to improve DTD times need evidence of patient benefit to justify long-term adoption. METHODS: We performed a retrospective study of patients who underwent endovascular thrombectomy for ischemic stroke. The likelihood of a favorable patient outcome was quantified for patients with a DTD time ≤90 minutes compared to patients with a DTD time >90 minutes. RESULTS: DTD ≤90 minutes was associated with an increased odds of having a more favorable (0-2) modified Rankin Score at 90-days (AOR, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.15-2.00; P = .004) post stroke compared to DTD >90 minutes. We did not find that DTD under or over 90 minutes had a significant association with discharge home (AOR, 1.21; 95% CI, 1.00-1.46; P = .051) or patients' length of stay (β, -0.48; 95% CI, -1.30-0.34; P = .20). CONCLUSIONS: Our study supports that EVT completed with DTD time ≤90 minutes was associated with better functional outcomes for patients.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: The American Heart Association (AHA) has a current goal of performing 50% of endovascular therapy (EVT) procedures with a door-to-device (DTD) time of 90 minutes or less for direct arriving patients. Initiatives to improve DTD times need evidence of patient benefit to justify long-term adoption. METHODS: We performed a retrospective study of patients who underwent endovascular thrombectomy for ischemic stroke.

title: Hypoxia and right ventricular dysfunction in patients with acute pulmonary embolism.
abstract: BACKGROUND: In patients with acute pulmonary embolism (PE), hypoxia may increase pulmonary vascular resistance and worsen right ventricular dysfunction (RVD), which is a key prognostic factor. However, associations between hypoxia, RVD and clinical outcomes have not been well described. AIM: To describe associations between hypoxia, RVD and clinical outcomes in patients with PE. METHODS: We performed a retrospective, single-center cohort study of patients treated by the Massachusetts General Hospital Pulmonary Embolism Response Team (PERT) from 10/2012 to 08/2021. Inclusion criteria included confirmed PE, recorded oxygen saturation prior to PERT activation, and echocardiogram within three days of PERT activation. Patients were categorized into four subgroups based on (1) hypoxia status (SaO₂ below vs. above 95%) and, (2) oxygen support (below vs. above 3 L/min). Our primary outcome was the presence of RVD on echocardiogram. Our secondary outcome was clinical deterioration within 7 days. RESULTS: We included 894 PE patients. The mean age was 61 (± 16 SD), 614/894 (69%) were hypoxic, and 624/894 (70%) had RVD on echocardiogram. Overall, hypoxic patients were more likely to have RVD than non-hypoxic patients (467/614 [76%] vs. 157/280 [56%], p < 0.0001). On subgroup analysis, RVD prevalence was highest in the "hypoxic with oxygen support ≥3L" group (n = 216/266, 81%) followed by the "not hypoxic with oxygen support ≥3L" group 53/70 (76%); 198/278 (71%) in the "hypoxic with oxygen support <3L" and 157/280 (56%) in the "not hypoxic with oxygen support <3L" groups. Clinical deterioration occurred in 199/894 (22%) patients and was more common in hypoxic patients than non-hypoxic patients (157/614 [26%] vs. 42/280 [15%], p < 0.0001), and most common in the "hypoxic with oxygen support ≥3L" subgroup 88/266 (33%). CONCLUSIONS: Hypoxia is associated with RVD and clinical deterioration in patients with PE. More research is needed to understand the risk associated with hypoxia and the physiology of supplemental oxygen support in PE. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

However, associations between hypoxia, RVD and clinical outcomes have not been well described. AIM: To describe associations between hypoxia, RVD and clinical outcomes in patients with PE.

title: A comparison of aspiration thrombectomy with catheter-directed thrombolysis in the management of Paget-Schroetter syndrome.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Acute subclavian vein thrombosis secondary to thoracic outlet syndrome (Paget-Schroetter syndrome [PSS]) requires the prompt clearing of thrombus from the subclavian vein through catheter-directed thrombolysis (CDT) or aspiration thrombectomy (ASP). Our goal is to systematically compare the outcomes of CDT and ASP in the management of PSS. METHODS: Consecutive patients with PSS at a single institution from 2020 through 2025 were reviewed for management with CDT or ASP. Venograms were assessed for patency, stenosis, and subclavian post-thrombotic changes (PTC). PTC were graded based on the degree of luminal encroachment and vessel irregularity: mild (<10%), moderate (10%-50%), and severe (50%-99%). Interventions were assessed: (1) within 1 week of the procedure, (2) before subclavian vein decompression, (3) 2 weeks after subclavian vein decompression, and (4) patency on the last venogram. Standardized outcomes were assessed. RESULTS: A total of 110 patients with PSS were treated over 5 years. Of these patients, 54 met the inclusion criteria: 28 underwent CDT and 26 underwent ASP. At 1 week following the procedure, rethrombosis occurred in 1 (3.6%) patient who underwent CDT and 6 (23.1%) patients who underwent ASP (P < .5). Failure to clear thrombosis occurred in 13.8% of patients who underwent ASP. The composite rate of early thrombosis and procedural failure was higher in the ASP cohort. Before PSS surgery, occlusion was noted in 1 (3.6%) patient who underwent CDT and 8 (30.8%) patients who underwent ASP (P < .05). PTC was mild in 13 (46.4%) patients receiving CDT and 5 (19.2%) receiving ASP (P < .05); moderate in 5 (17.9%) receiving CDT and 5 (19.2%) receiving ASP; and severe in 9 (32.1%) receiving CDT and 8 (30.8) receiving ASP. At early follow-up after PSS surgery, PTC was mild in 10 (43.5%) patients receiving CDT and 4 (23.5) receiving ASP; moderate in 2 (8.7%) receiving CDT and 1 (5.9%) receiving ASP; and severe in 9 (39.1%) receiving CDT and 6 (35.3%) receiving ASP. Occlusion was noted in 2 (8.7%) patients receiving CDT and 6 (35%) receiving ASP. Recanalization resulted in final patency in 22 (95%) patients receiving CDT and 15 (88%) receiving ASP. CONCLUSIONS: Both ASP and CDT may be employed for clearing thrombus in PSS; however, they differ in early efficacy, PTC, and patency. Our results suggest that while often more rapid and convenient, ASP may be inferior to CAT in the management of PSS.

Our goal is to systematically compare the outcomes of CDT and ASP in the management of PSS. METHODS: Consecutive patients with PSS at a single institution from 2020 through 2025 were reviewed for management with CDT or ASP.

title: Emerging precision techniques in technology-assisted customized endovascular management of thoracoabdominal aneurysms with anomalous arch branching.
abstract: Thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm (TAAA) repair is highly complex, especially in the presence of rare aortic arch branching anomalies that complicate fenestrated graft deployment. Emerging technologies such as robotic-assisted vascular surgery with haptic feedback and advanced imaging aim to improve precision and reduce technical errors in these challenging cases. Patient-specific 3D-printed vascular models further enhance preoperative planning and intraoperative navigation by improving anatomical understanding in complex arch variants. Spinal cord ischemia remains a major complication after TAAA repair, and reduced operative time through minimally invasive and robotic-assisted approaches may potentially lower this risk, although evidence is still limited. While these innovations show promise in improving surgical accuracy and efficiency, robust multicenter studies are needed to validate their effectiveness and define their role in standard clinical practice.

title: Long-Term Safety and Efficacy of Upadacitinib in Patients with Psoriatic Arthritis: 5-Year Results from the Phase 3 SELECT-PsA 1 Study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: In the phase 3 SELECT-PsA 1 study, treatment with upadacitinib (UPA), an oral Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor, improved signs and symptoms of psoriatic arthritis (PsA) from weeks 12 through 152. We now report the long-term extension phase, evaluating safety and efficacy of upadacitinib versus adalimumab (ADA) up to week 260 (~ 5 years). METHODS: Data on treatment-emergent adverse events and all primary and secondary endpoints were collected through week 260 for patients who received a placebo or ≥ 1 dose of UPA at either 15 mg (UPA15) or 30 mg (UPA30) daily, or ADA 40 mg every other week. For non-radiographic binary endpoints, both observed data and non-responder imputation methods were used, whereas for radiographic binary endpoints, the observed data method was used. For continuous endpoints, observed data and mixed-effects model repeated-measures analyses were employed. RESULTS: A total of 1704 patients received at least one dose of study drug, with 983 (57.7%) completing 260 weeks of treatment. The safety profile of UPA through week 260 was consistent with data from weeks 104 and 152. UPA treatment was associated with higher rates of serious infections, herpes zoster, lymphopenia, creatine kinase elevation, and non-melanoma skin cancer compared with ADA treatment. The exposure-adjusted incidence rates for major adverse cardiovascular events (n/100 PY [95% CI]: UPA15, 0.4 [0.2, 0.8]; UPA30, 0.4 [0.1, 0.9]; ADA, 0.3 [0.1, 0.7]) and venous thromboembolism (UPA15, 0.2 [0.0, 0.5]; UPA30, 0.4 [0.1, 0.9]; ADA, 0.2 [0.0, 0.6]) were low and comparable across treatment groups. Efficacy improvements observed with UPA at weeks 56 and 104 were maintained through week 260 and were comparable to those achieved with ADA. CONCLUSIONS: The safety profile of UPA over 5 years remained consistent with that observed at weeks 104 and 152, with no new signals identified. title: Beyond Absolute Blood Pressure Targets During Endovascular Thrombectomy: A Narrative Review of Intraprocedural Hemodynamics.
abstract: Hemodynamic management is a central component of procedural care for acute ischemic stroke (AIS) during endovascular thrombectomy (EVT). Current guideline recommendations predominantly provide absolute blood pressure (BP) targets for intraprocedural management. Studies have also examined relative BP reduction, the magnitude and duration of hypotensive exposure, and blood pressure variability (BPV), providing additional measures of systemic hemodynamic exposure during EVT. However, definitions, baseline reference pressures, measurement intervals, and BPV metrics vary widely across studies, and associations with neurological outcomes are inconsistent. Importantly, these systemic BP parameters do not directly establish cerebral perfusion. This limitation supports investigating cerebral autoregulation as a complementary, patient-specific assessment. Evidence linking individualized autoregulatory limits to outcomes remains predominantly post-EVT, with very limited evidence during the pre-recanalization phase under anesthesia. This review examines intraprocedural BP during EVT under anesthesia beyond absolute pressure targets. It considers relative BP reduction, the magnitude and duration of hypotensive exposure, pressure-time burden, BPV, and individualized autoregulatory limits in relation to cerebral perfusion. A narrative literature search was conducted in PubMed for studies evaluating hemodynamics during EVT under anesthesia, supplemented by screening of selected reference lists. Studies examining intraprocedural BP targets, relative changes, hypotension duration, pressure-time burden, and BPV in relation to neurological or imaging outcomes under anesthesia were prioritized, with emphasis on the pre-recanalization period. Post-EVT hemodynamic studies were not included in the primary synthesis, except where they informed the discussion of cerebral autoregulation and future research. Intraprocedural hemodynamic variables during EVT characterize different aspects of systemic arterial-pressure exposure that may be relevant to cerebral perfusion in the ischemic penumbra. Absolute pressure, relative change, magnitude and duration of hypotension, pressure-time burden, and BPV should be regarded as complementary rather than interchangeable measures. Differences in reference pressures, definitions, measurement intervals, exposure periods relative to recanalization, and anesthesia techniques limit comparisons and standardization across studies. Future prospective studies, particularly during general anesthesia (GA), should integrate clearly defined systemic BP metrics with dynamic cerebral autoregulation. This may help determine which parameters or combinations best reflect cerebral physiological vulnerability. Individualized autoregulation-guided BP targets remain investigational and require prospective validation before they can inform routine clinical hemodynamic management.

Current guideline recommendations predominantly provide absolute blood pressure (BP) targets for intraprocedural management. Studies have also examined relative BP reduction, the magnitude and duration of hypotensive exposure, and blood pressure variability (BPV), providing additional measures of systemic hemodynamic exposure during EVT.

title: Endovascular repair of iatrogenic popliteal artery injury with acute limb ischemia during unicompartmental knee arthroplasty.
abstract: Iatrogenic popliteal artery injury is a rare but severe complication of knee arthroplasty. A 75-year-old woman developed massive bleeding and acute limb ischemia during unicompartmental knee arthroplasty. Angiography showed severe popliteal flow impairment with thrombus and absent distal runoff. Because bleeding was controlled and guidewire crossing appeared feasible, an endovascular-first strategy was chosen. After successful crossing, an intravascular ultrasound scan confirmed severe arterial wall disruption and an adequate distal landing zone. VIABAHN stent grafts excluded the injured segment, and tibial thrombus aspiration restored distal perfusion. The patient was discharged without gait impairment. Endovascular-first treatment may be effective in selected patients.

A 75-year-old woman developed massive bleeding and acute limb ischemia during unicompartmental knee arthroplasty. Angiography showed severe popliteal flow impairment with thrombus and absent distal runoff.

title: Perioperative management of DOAC in elective orthopedic surgery: a prospective cohort analysis.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Treatment with direct oral anticoagulants is usually interrupted prior to surgery to reduce bleeding risk. Current guidelines recommend standardized interruption protocols, but the actual preoperative plasma levels and their clinical implications in real-world surgical populations are not well characterized. The aim of this study was to assess preoperative DOAC plasma concentrations and postoperative bleeding and thromboembolic outcomes in patients undergoing elective orthopedic surgery. METHODS: We conducted a prospective observational study at Danderyd Hospital, Stockholm, Sweden. Adults (≥ 18 years) treated with apixaban, rivaroxaban, or dabigatran for atrial fibrillation or venous thromboembolism and scheduled for high-bleeding-risk orthopedic procedures were included. DOAC interruption followed national guidelines. Plasma DOAC levels were measured preoperatively using LC-MS/MS. Clinical outcomes, including bleeding and thromboembolic events, were recorded up to 30 days postoperatively. RESULTS: A total of 54 patients receiving ongoing DOAC therapy (mean age, 75.5 years; 54% male) were included, of whom 87% were on apixaban. Plasma DOAC concentrations had a mean of 6.7 ng/mL (range, <1.9 to 23.1 ng/mL), and 38% of patients had levels below the limit of detection (< 2.0 ng/mL). One patient had a concentration >30 ng/mL. Five patients (16%) experienced clinically relevant non-major bleeding; four of these had undetectable DOAC levels. No major bleeding, thromboembolic events, or deaths were observed. CONCLUSIONS: Standardized interruption protocols for DOAC therapy result in low or undetectable plasma levels in most patients undergoing high-risk elective orthopedic surgery. Routine preoperative DOAC level testing appears unnecessary in the general population but may be valuable in subgroups at high risk of bleeding.

title: One-year outcomes of mechanical thrombectomy and catheter-directed thrombolysis in acute pulmonary embolism.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Although anticoagulation remains the standard of care for acute pulmonary embolism (PE), mechanical thrombectomy (MT) and catheter-directed thrombolysis (CDT) have emerged as effective interventional options for rapid clot removal. However, their comparative outcomes remain incompletely defined. Hence, this study compared the outcomes of MT and CDT for acute PE at a tertiary referral center in the United States. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of all patients who underwent MT or CDT for acute PE across a single hospital system between January 2021 and April 2025. Patients were stratified into MT and CDT groups based on the treatment received. Baseline characteristics, procedural data, and clinical outcomes were analyzed. The primary outcome was 30-day mortality. The secondary outcomes included length of hospital stay, major adverse events, reintervention, and PE recurrence. Patients were followed up for up to 1 year or until death. RESULTS: A total of 724 patients were included in this study: 569 (79%) underwent MT and 155 (21%) received CDT. The mean age was 63 ± 16 years, and 49% were female. Most patients (76%) were classified as intermediate-high risk, with a mean right ventricle to left ventricle ratio of 1.5 ± 0.5. Bilateral or saddle embolism was present in 93% of patients. Patients in the MT group were more likely to have a simplified PE severity index of >0 (73% vs 60%; P < .001). Age and the rates of cancer, chronic cardiopulmonary disease, and concurrent deep vein thrombosis were similar between the groups. The median procedure duration was longer for MT (66 minutes, interquartile range, 46-89) than for CDT (58 minutes, interquartile range, 40-77; P = .003). The median postoperative length of stay was 3 days in both groups. MT was associated with a higher incidence of intraoperative adverse cardiac events (2.5% vs 0%; P = .048), and CDT was associated with higher intensive care unit admission rates (83% vs 36%; P < .001). However, the 30-day mortality rate was similar between the groups (CDT: 2.6% vs MT: 4.6%; P = .27). Additionally, the 1-year incidence rates of chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (MT: 4.5% vs CDT: 3.4%; P = .69), PE recurrence (MT: 4.4% vs CDT: 2.5%; P = .31), and all-cause mortality (MT: 7.8% vs CDT: 5.8%; P = .41) were not statistically significantly different between the MT and CDT groups. CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective cohort, MT and CDT for acute PE showed statistically comparable 30-day mortality rates and 1-year recurrence rates of chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension and PE. MT was associated with a higher incidence of intraoperative cardiac complications, and CDT was associated with more frequent intensive care unit admission.

However, their comparative outcomes remain incompletely defined. Hence, this study compared the outcomes of MT and CDT for acute PE at a tertiary referral center in the United States.

title: A Compact Unified Model for Moderate-to-Severe Carotid Artery Stenosis Using Image Segmentation: A Multicenter Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of a new artificial intelligence model, the compact unified model (CU-Model), for moderate-to-severe carotid artery stenosis using digital subtraction angiography (DSA) images compared to clinical reference standards. METHODS: In this retrospective multicenter study, 156 patients with confirmed moderate-to-severe carotid artery stenosis were included. A pretrained CU-Model (trained on public non-clinical datasets for optical flow and stereo matching) was applied to raw DSA images without any fine-tuning on clinical data to avoid data leakage. The model served exclusively as a post-acquisition support tool: cardiologists applied it immediately after procedures for automated vessel segmentation and highlighting. Final North American Symptomatic Carotid Endarterectomy Trial (NASCET) measurements and interpreta-tions were performed manually under expert supervision by 2 blinded researchers. RESULTS: The CU-Model identified left internal carotid artery (ICA) stenosis in 84 patients and right ICA stenosis in 72. It misclassified only 1 moderate left ICA stenosis case as normal, achieving 99.4% sensitivity (155/156) for any stenosis detection. For stenosis severity grading, strong agreement with DSA was observed (moderate: 57.68 ± 5.94 vs. 57.71 ± 6.19, r = 0.83, P < .001, 95% CI: 0.76-0.88; severe: 86.96 ± 5.97 vs. 87.02 ± 6.18, r = 0.91, P < .001, 95% CI: 0.85-0.95). Of 156 cases, 106 were moderate (50%-69%) and 50 severe (≥70%), using NASCET-adapted thresholds accounting for measurement variability. Hypertension (77%), smoking, and syncope were common, with significant association in symptomatic patients (P < .05). CONCLUSION: The CU-Model demonstrates strong concordance with DSA as a practical, post-procedure support tool for vessel segmentation. Pending larger validation studies, it shows promise for enhancing clinical workflow efficiency.

title: Emergency management of postoperative airway obstruction following carotid endarterectomy: a systematic review.
abstract: Postoperative airway obstruction after carotid endarterectomy presents a significant challenge to anaesthetists. Airway oedema, with or without haematoma, may rapidly develop with life-threatening consequences. This systematic review aims to inform best practice in the management of postoperative airway obstruction following carotid endarterectomy. A literature search was conducted for manuscripts published between 01/01/2000 and 01/07/2025. Articles describing the anaesthetic management of adult patients who developed postoperative airway obstruction following carotid endarterectomy were included. Reference lists of the reviewed articles were also scrutinised for additional relevant sources. Outcome measures were the presentation of airway obstruction, success rate of airway interventions, duration of tracheal intubation and incidence of airway-related morbidity and mortality. Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. The literature search yielded 284 articles, of which 32 full papers were reviewed. Six papers were deemed pertinent, in addition to five identified from review of references, for a total of 11 included in this systematic review (five case reports, three case series and three retrospective observational studies) detailing the management of airway compromise post-carotid endarterectomy in 84 cases. Clinical signs correlate poorly with anatomical distortion, and laryngeal oedema is generally more severe than anticipated. Prompt haematoma evacuation improved the success rate of airway management, without associated morbidity or mortality. Surgical exploration under local anaesthesia was efficacious and may avoid the need for airway intervention. Awake tracheal intubation was associated with fewer complications than asleep tracheal intubation and should be considered where time and patient cooperation allow. Emergency front-of-neck access should not be delayed for repeated attempts at tracheal intubation with a high chance of failure. Patients' tracheas should remain intubated for sufficient time after surgical exploration, allowing airway oedema to resolve prior to extubation.

title: Higher fibrosis-4 index is associated with 1-year in-stent restenosis after carotid artery stenting.
abstract: BACKGROUND: In-stent restenosis (ISR) is a clinically important complication of carotid artery stenting (CAS); however, practical risk markers remain understudied. Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is associated with atherosclerotic risk, and the Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index, a non-invasive marker of liver fibrosis, has been linked to carotid atherosclerosis progression. Therefore, this study examined whether the FIB-4 index was associated with ISR after CAS. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 132 patients who underwent CAS between 2010 and 2023. ISR was defined as peak systolic velocity ≥175 cm/s on at least two consecutive duplex examinations. The primary analysis evaluated FIB-4 continuously per 1-SD increase using Cox models. Secondary exploratory analyses used a cohort-derived cutoff determined by the Youden index. RESULTS: ISR occurred in 16/132 (12%) patients. When analyzed continuously, FIB-4 was not significantly associated with ISR in univariable analysis (HR per 1-SD increase, 1.34; 95% CI, 0.88-2.04; p = 0.172) or in a parsimonious model adjusted for sex and stent design (adjusted HR, 1.40; 95% CI, 0.89-2.21; p = 0.142). The cohort-derived cutoff was 2.08. In secondary exploratory analysis, FIB-4 ≥ 2.08 was associated with higher ISR risk after adjustment for sex and stent design (adjusted HR, 3.93; 95% CI, 1.42-10.9; p = 0.008). CONCLUSIONS: Although continuous FIB-4 was not significantly associated with ISR, exploratory cutoff-based analyses suggested an association between higher FIB-4 and 1-year ISR after CAS. Further validation is required before clinical use.

title: Proton pump inhibitor use was not associated with reduced gastrointestinal bleeding risk in ischemic stroke patients treated with dual antiplatelet therapy.
abstract: BACKGROUND: To evaluate the association between proton pump inhibitor (PPI) use and gastrointestinal bleeding (GIB) in acute ischemic stroke (AIS) patients receiving dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT). METHODS: This retrospective study analyzed 3,122 AIS patients with large artery atherosclerosis (LAA) treated with DAPT at Qingdao University Affiliated Hospital (September 2020-December 2023). Adjusted odds ratios (aORs) for GIB were calculated using binary logistic regression, controlling for confounders including age, sex, and other baseline characteristics. To address confounding by indication, we additionally performed 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM) as a sensitivity analysis, with conditional logistic regression applied to the matched cohort. RESULTS: 45.0% (n = 1,404) received concomitant PPI. No significant difference in GIB incidence was observed between PPI users and non-PPI users (2.1% vs. 1.3%, p = 0.12). Subgroup analyses revealed that PPI use was significantly associated with increased GIB risk in non-endovascular therapy patients (aOR = 2.08, p = 0.03), particularly those with posterior circulation infarction (aOR = 5.96, p = 0.006). These findings were further supported by propensity score matching analysis (conditional OR = 1.64, 95% CI 0.87-3.09, p = 0.124 for the overall cohort; conditional OR = 12.29, 95% CI 1.59-94.90, p = 0.016 for posterior circulation infarction in the non-endovascular subgroup). No significant association between PPI use and GIB risk was found in endovascular therapy or age-stratified subgroups. CONCLUSION: PPI use was not associated with reduced overall GIB risk in DAPT-treated AIS patients. Routine PPI prophylaxis may be unnecessary for low-bleeding-risk populations, while the association observed in posterior circulation infarction remains hypothesis-generating and warrants prospective validation.

Adjusted odds ratios (aORs) for GIB were calculated using binary logistic regression, controlling for confounders including age, sex, and other baseline characteristics.

title: Selective endovascular aortic repair in connective tissue disease patients within a multidisciplinary program achieves comparable outcomes in high-risk patients.
abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVE: Endovascular aortic repair (ENDO) in patients with connective tissue disease (CTD) has historically been discouraged in society guidelines because of durability concerns. However, high-volume aortic centers increasingly employ ENDO strategies in carefully selected high-risk patients across scenarios such as rupture, dissection-related pathology, or hostile anatomy. Herein, we describe temporal ENDO adoption at our multidisciplinary CTD aortic program. METHODS: In this study, 92 patients with CTD undergoing aortic intervention at a single high-volume aortic center between 2005 and 2023 were analyzed. Patients were stratified by ENDO (n = 50) vs open repair (OPEN; n = 42). The primary outcome was freedom from aortic-related mortality (ARM). The secondary outcomes included technical success, complications, secondary aortic intervention (SAI), and overall survival. A prespecified contemporary analysis (2018-2023) was conducted to evaluate the outcomes following the establishment of a multidisciplinary CTD aortic program. The Kaplan-Meier method was used to estimate survival and freedom from SAI. RESULTS: The mean age was 48 ± 16 years, and 34% (n = 31) were female. Diagnoses included Marfan syndrome (69%), Loeys-Dietz syndrome (15%), familial aortopathy (11%), and vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (5%). Patients who underwent ENDO more frequently had prior sternotomy/open cardiac surgery (68% vs 19%; P < .0001), prior aortic surgery (70% vs 33%; P = .0007), and urgent presentation (50% vs 14%; P = .0004). Overall, 60% of these patients were deemed unfit for open repair by the multidisciplinary aortic team because of physiologic risk, anatomic complexity, or urgent presentation. The technical success rate was lower after ENDO (82% vs 98%; P = .02), and the 30-day reintervention rate was higher (16% vs 0%; P = .01). The median follow-up period was 2.3 years [interquartile range, 1.1-4.7]. SAIs occurred more frequently following ENDO (56% vs 12%; P = .0001), including planned staged procedures (ENDO: 28.6% vs OPEN: 20%; P = 1) and unplanned reinterventions (ENDO: 71.4% vs OPEN: 80%; P = 1). In the full cohort, patients undergoing ENDO had lower 3-year survival rates (71% ± 7% vs 92% ± 4%; log-rank P = .03). In the contemporary cohort, survival at 2 years following ENDO (n = 17) was poorer than that after OPEN (n = 42), although the difference did not reach significance (71% ± 14% vs 92% ± 4%; log-rank P = .1). Similarly, the rate of freedom from ARM was lower, but not significantly different (88% ± 12% vs 98% ± 2%; log-rank P = .4). CONCLUSIONS: Open repair remains the gold standard for connective tissue disease-associated aortic disease. In carefully selected high-risk patients, ENDO serves as a complementary strategy with acceptable contemporary survival and comparable freedom from ARM. Higher secondary intervention rates reflect both planned staged repair and unplanned surveillance-detected failure modes, underscoring the need for lifelong follow-up within multidisciplinary programs.

However, high-volume aortic centers increasingly employ ENDO strategies in carefully selected high-risk patients across scenarios such as rupture, dissection-related pathology, or hostile anatomy. Herein, we describe temporal ENDO adoption at our multidisciplinary CTD aortic program.

title: Chocolate Balloon Versus Conventional Balloon for Vessel Preparation Before Drug-Coated Balloon Angioplasty in Femoropopliteal Lesions: A Real-World Propensity Score-Matched Study.
abstract: To evaluate the procedural and 1-year clinical outcomes of the Chocolate balloon versus conventional plain old balloon angioplasty (POBA) for vessel preparation before drug-coated balloon (DCB) treatment of femoropopliteal lesions. This retrospective subgroup analysis of the multicenter PROMISING registry included patients with femoropopliteal lesions treated with DCB. Before propensity score matching (PSM), 817 patients underwent POBA and 379 underwent Chocolate balloon angioplasty. After 1:1 PSM, 254 patients were included in each group. The primary endpoint was bailout stenting. Secondary endpoints included maximum DCB diameter, stent length, postprocedural ankle-brachial index (ABI), 1-year clinically driven target lesion revascularization (CD-TLR), major amputation, all-cause mortality, amputation-free survival (AFS), and major adverse events (MAE). After PSM, bailout stenting occurred less frequently in the Chocolate balloon group than in the POBA group (20.47% vs 29.92%, p = 0.014). The Chocolate balloon group also showed a trend toward shorter stent length (20.67 ± 9.75 cm vs 23.71 ± 10.62 cm, p = 0.097) and allowed use of larger DCBs (4.96 ± 0.52 mm vs 4.74 ± 0.61 mm, p < 0.001). Multivariable logistic regression identified Chocolate balloon use as an independent protective factor against bailout stenting, whereas chronic total occlusion and severe calcification were independent predictors of bailout stenting. No significant differences were observed in 1-year clinical outcomes. Compared with POBA, Chocolate balloon vessel preparation reduced bailout stenting and enabled use of larger DCBs, suggesting potential procedural advantages in complex femoropopliteal lesions. However, these procedural benefits did not translate into improved 1-year clinical outcomes.

Before propensity score matching (PSM), 817 patients underwent POBA and 379 underwent Chocolate balloon angioplasty.

title: Closing the Gap in Thromboprophylaxis: A Multidisciplinary Quality Improvement Approach Among Medical Inpatients.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the impact of a multidisciplinary quality improvement (QI) framework on guideline-directed venous thromboembolism (VTE) prophylaxis adherence among hospitalized patients. STUDY DESIGN: A prospective, pre-post interventional study conducted in internal medicine wards with historically low baseline prophylaxis rates. METHODS: Following a retrospective baseline assessment, a multicomponent QI initiative was executed across 2 Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles in adult internal medicine wards at a university hospital between September and November 2022. Interventions included the following: (1) physician education on the Padua Prediction Score and International Medical Prevention Registry on Venous Thromboembolism Bleeding Risk Score; (2) implementation of an electronic health record clinical decision-support tool prompting VTE risk assessments; and (3) integration of clinical pharmacists into daily multidisciplinary rounds to provide active audit and feedback. RESULTS: At baseline, 62.1% of high-risk patients received guideline-recommended VTE prophylaxis. Post intervention, this rate increased to 79.1% in the first cycle and 82.1% in the second cycle ( P  = .006). Among clinical pharmacists' 27 recommendations, 70.4% were accepted and implemented. The multidimensional strategy demonstrated sustained improvements in guideline adherence with minimal adverse events. CONCLUSIONS: Implementing a multidisciplinary QI framework significantly enhanced guideline-directed VTE prophylaxis use among hospitalized patients. This collaborative approach underscores the value of electronic decision support, clinical audit-feedback loops, and pharmacist-physician integration in driving patient safety. Ultimately, this system-level strategy provides a scalable model for improving preventive care protocols across diverse hospital settings.

title: Temporal Net Water Uptake Evolution and Its Association with Functional Outcome in Acute Ischemic Stroke.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Subacute lesion growth after acute ischemic stroke (AIS) is associated with worse functional outcomes. The ischemic lesion severity can be assessed with net water uptake (NWU), a CT-based marker of edema. Pretreatment NWU has been associated with worse functional outcomes; however, it remains unclear how the temporal changes in NWU influence functional outcomes. In this study, we aimed to determine how associations between NWU and functional outcome vary across imaging times up to 1 week after stroke. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We included patients from the Multicenter Randomized Clinical Trial of Endovascular Treatment for Acute Ischemic Stroke in the Netherlands (MRCLEAN-NO IV) trial with anterior circulation large vessel occlusion who were treated with endovascular treatment and had baseline, 24-hour, and 1-week follow-up noncontrast CT scans. Functional outcome at 90 days was evaluated using the mRS, analyzed both as functional independence (mRS 0-2) and across the full ordinal distribution (mRS 0-6). In the primary analysis, associations between NWU measured at different imaging time points and functional independence were examined using univariable and multivariable logistic regression models. To evaluate temporal changes in NWU, ΔNWU was calculated at different time intervals (baseline to 24 hours, 24 hours to 1 week, and baseline to 1 week), and its association with outcomes was analyzed using analogous regression models. RESULTS: 1wk-BL Of 539 MRCLEAN-NO IV patients, 115 were included in this study. The median time from stroke onset to randomization was 92 (IQR, 70-140) minutes. The median NWU evolved from 4.3% (interquartile range [IQR], 2.1%-6.8%) at baseline to 9.0% (IQR, 3.0%-13%) at 24 hours and 15% (IQR, 11%-19%) at 1 week. The median patient-level change (ΔNWU) from baseline to 1 week was 10% (IQR, 5.3%-16%). NWU measured at 1 week, but not at baseline or 24 hours, was significantly associated with functional dependence, with an adjusted OR (aOR) of 0.66 (95% CI, 0.47-0.90) per 5-percentage-point increase in NWU. Furthermore, a higher increase in NWU from baseline to 1-week imaging was significantly associated with functional dependence, with an aOR of 0.66 (95% CI, 0.47-0.86) per 5-percentage-point increase in ΔNWU. CONCLUSIONS: In our population, NWU measured at 1 week is associated with 90-day clinical outcomes, suggesting that lesion evolution continues in the first week after stroke onset and may therefore represent a target for secondary treatments to improve clinical outcomes.

The ischemic lesion severity can be assessed with net water uptake (NWU), a CT-based marker of edema. Pretreatment NWU has been associated with worse functional outcomes; however, it remains unclear how the temporal changes in NWU influence functional outcomes.

title: Impact of direct-to-operating room transfer protocol for ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the impact of a direct-to-operating room (DOR) transfer protocol for ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm (rAAA) on surgical volume, interhospital transfer patterns, and surgical outcomes at a tertiary referral center. METHODS: P This retrospective, single-institution cohort study used institutional databases and the Vascular Quality Initiative registry to identify all patients undergoing rAAA repair between 2014 and 2024. In January 2020, a multidisciplinary rapid-response transfer protocol was implemented to facilitate DOR transfers. Patients were stratified into pre- and postimplementation cohorts. Differences in case volume, transfer patterns, transfer distance, time to treatment, and surgical outcomes between groups were assessed using univariable analysis, with statistical significance set at< .05. RESULTS: P P P P P P A total of 96 patients underwent rAAA repair during the study period, with 28.1% treated before and 71.9% treated after implementation of the transfer protocol. Baseline characteristics were similar between cohorts, except for a higher prevalence of diabetes (40.7% vs 14.5%;= .005) and former smokers (59.3% vs 34.8%;= .029) in the preimplementation group. The annual rAAA repair volume increased threefold after implementation, from a mean of 4.5 to 13.8 cases/year. Overall, 86.5% of patients were transferred from outside hospitals, with a significant increase in the proportion of external transfers after implementation (70.4% vs 92.8%;= .007). Median transfer distance increased from 23.7 to 49.1 miles (= .017) and time from transfer acceptance to operating room arrival decreased from 173 to 124 minutes (= .145). Distance-adjusted transfer time decreased significantly from 9.5 to 4.1 min/mile (= .017). Endovascular repair was performed in 68.8% of patients, with no difference between cohorts. In-hospital stroke (6.2%), myocardial infarction (7.3%), and mortality (22.9%) rates were similar between groups. Median length of stay was 6.6 days. Thirty-day outcomes did not differ between cohorts, with readmission in 13.5%, reintervention in 36.5%, and mortality in 25.0% of patients. CONCLUSIONS: Implementation of a multidisciplinary DOR protocol for rAAA was associated with a sustained increase in surgical volume, higher rates of interhospital transfer, expansion of the regional referral network, and lower distance-adjusted transfer times, with perioperative outcomes remaining within contemporary benchmarks.

title: Drug-Eluting Resorbable Scaffolds for Infrapopliteal Peripheral Artery Disease: A State-of-the-Art Review.
abstract: Drug-eluting resorbable scaffolds (DRS) have been developed to overcome the key limitations of conventional endovascular therapies for below-the-knee (BTK) peripheral artery disease (PAD), including acute recoil, restenosis, and the sequela of long-term permanent metallic implants. DRS provides a temporary mechanical support and localized antiproliferative drug delivery after which the scaffold is gradually resorbed, ultimately restoring native vessel architecture to preserve future revascularization options. Over the past decade, numerous prospective and observational studies have evaluated both polymer- and magnesium alloy-based DRS platforms and have demonstrated favorable patency, wound healing, and limb salvage outcomes in patients with advanced infrapopliteal PAD. Most recently, randomized evidence from the LIFE-BTK trial has demonstrated superior patency and reduced rates of revascularization with DRS-treated lesions as compared with plain balloon angioplasty. In this state-of-the-art review, we summarize the existing evidence evaluating DRS devices for BTK PAD and present an updated systematic review and meta-analysis of clinical outcomes for DRS-based endovascular interventions.

title: Incremental prognostic and risk-stratification value of ultrasound-based Carotid Plaque Reporting and Data System (Plaque-RADS) classification for recurrent ischemic stroke in patients with low-to-moderate-grade carotid stenosis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The Carotid Plaque Reporting and Data System (Plaque-RADS) is a system for stroke risk assessment. However, the clinical utility of ultrasound (US)-based Plaque-RADS remains unclear. This study aimed to assess the incremental prognostic value and risk stratification utility of US-based Plaque-RADS in patients with prior stroke and low-to-moderate-grade carotid stenosis. METHODS: Between January 2020 and December 2022, 231 patients with carotid plaque ipsilateral to the prior stroke and low-to-moderate-grade carotid stenosis were retrospectively screened, of whom 158 were included in the final analysis. US-based Plaque-RADS classification was assigned based on duplex US assessment of plaque features. Cox regression and subgroup analyses were performed to evaluate the association between high-risk US-based Plaque-RADS categories and recurrent ischemic stroke. Model discrimination was assessed using receiver operating characteristic curves and area under the curve (AUC), and clinical utility was evaluated using decision curve analysis. The association between increasing US-based Plaque-RADS categories and the risk of recurrent ischemic stroke was assessed by trend analysis. The incremental risk-stratification value of refined high-risk Plaque-RADS thresholds was quantified with net reclassification improvement (NRI) and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI). Internal validation was performed using bootstrap resampling. RESULTS: vs. During the 3-year follow-up period, recurrent ischemic stroke occurred in 33 patients. High-risk US-based Plaque-RADS categories were significantly associated with recurrent ischemic stroke in patients with prior stroke and low-to-moderate-grade carotid stenosis, after adjusting for smoking, homocysteine, and intraplaque neovascularization [adjusted hazard ratio: 3.56; 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.07-11.83, P=0.038]. No statistically significant interactions were observed across the subgroups (all P for interaction >0.05). The Plaque-RADS ≥3 model demonstrated a higher AUC than the conventional US model [0.816 (95% CI: 0.731-0.901)0.810 (95% CI: 0.720-0.899)] and provided a slight net benefit across selected threshold probabilities. Additionally, the risk of recurrent ischemic stroke increased with higher Plaque-RADS categories (P for trend <0.001). Among the models using different high-risk Plaque-RADS thresholds, the Plaque-RADS ≥3b model showed the best predictive performance (0.865, 95% CI: 0.799-0.930), compared with the Plaque-RADS ≥3 model and the Plaque-RADS ≥3c model [0.824 (95% CI: 0.740-0.906)]. The Plaque-RADS ≥3b model also showed moderate improvements in NRI [0.250; (95% CI: 0.088-0.557), P=0.017] and IDI [0.090; (95% CI: 0.000-0.185), P=0.049], compared with the Plaque-RADS ≥3 model. Bootstrap internal validation indicated limited optimism across all models. CONCLUSIONS: In patients with prior stroke and low-to-moderate-grade carotid stenosis, high-risk US-based Plaque-RADS categories were significantly associated with recurrent ischemic stroke. The US-based Plaque-RADS may help identify plaque phenotypes associated with an increased risk of recurrent ipsilateral ischemic stroke, while refined high-risk thresholds, particularly Plaque-RADS ≥3b, may provide additional value for risk stratification.

title: Time-zero multimodal risk stratification for in-hospital mortality in acute aortic dissection: two-centre development, temporal and external validation, and occult shock phenotyping.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute aortic dissection (AAD) requires rapid anatomical diagnosis and early risk stratification, yet initial blood pressure alone may miss patients with concealed hypoperfusion. Although computed tomography angiography (CTA) defines dissection anatomy and transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) provides bedside haemodynamic information, the incremental prognostic value of early TTE and the significance of normotensive hyperlactatemia remain uncertain. We aimed to develop and validate an initial 2-hour multimodal model integrating clinical, CTA, and TTE data to predict in-hospital mortality and to describe occult shock in normotensive AAD patients. METHODS: This retrospective two-centre cohort study included 2,584 adults with first-time AAD who completed CTA and TTE during the initial 2-hour assessment after emergency department triage. Cohorts were development (n=1,678; 2007-2017), internal temporal validation (n=452; 2018-2021), and external geographic/later-era validation (n=454; 2022-March 2024). Candidate variables were restricted to information available during this initial assessment window. Four supervised algorithms were compared, with ablation analyses assessing modality-specific contribution. RESULTS: XGBoost achieved optimism-corrected development area under the curve (AUC) of 0.86 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.82-0.88], internal validation 0.83 (0.79-0.87), and external validation 0.78 (0.74-0.82). Adding TTE to Clinical + CTA improved discrimination (Delta AUC +0.04, P=0.002) and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI) (+0.021, P=0.01). Normotensive occult shock occurred in 548/2,082 patients (26.3%) and was associated with mortality 15.9% versus 6.7% in metabolically stable normotension. CONCLUSIONS: In high-volume aortic centres where CTA and early TTE are routinely available, this initial 2-hour multimodal model showed temporal validation and moderate external discrimination for in-hospital mortality. TTE added prognostic information, particularly for type A disease, and normotensive hyperlactatemia identified a higher-risk subgroup; however, general use, type B performance, local recalibration, and action thresholds require prospective multicentre validation before clinical implementation.

title: Impact of different follow-up methods on prognosis of diabetic foot patients after endovascular treatment: a multicenter retrospective cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) is a severe complication of diabetes mellitus, and endovascular treatment (EVT) has become the primary revascularization strategy. However, the impact of different post-procedure follow-up methods on clinical outcomes remains unclear. This study aimed to compare the effects of seven different follow-up approaches on prognosis in DFU patients after EVT. METHODS: This multicenter retrospective cohort study was conducted at three tertiary hospitals in China between June 2022 and June 2025. A total of 868 DFU patients who underwent successful EVT were enrolled and categorized into seven groups based on their primary follow-up method. The primary outcomes were 12-month wound healing rate and amputation-free survival (AFS). Secondary outcomes included major adverse limb events (MALE), reintervention rate, patient satisfaction, and glycemic control. Multivariable Cox regression and propensity score matching were used to adjust for confounders. RESULTS: Among 868 patients, the surgical hospital outpatient group demonstrated the highest 12-month wound healing rate (75.0%) and AFS rate (80.1%). The no follow-up group had the poorest outcomes (45.2% wound healing, 56.4% AFS). No follow-up was associated with significantly increased risk of MALE [adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) 2.15, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.62-2.85]. WeChat follow-up (aHR 1.22, 95% CI: 0.88-1.69) showed non-significant differences compared with surgical hospital outpatient follow-up. CONCLUSIONS: Structured follow-up significantly improves wound healing and AFS in DFU patients after EVT. Digital health tools such as WeChat showed no statistically significant difference compared with traditional follow-up, but these observational data should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalent effectiveness. The absence of follow-up is associated with substantially worse outcomes. These findings are hypothesis-generating and warrant validation in prospective randomized trials.

title: PERT implementation and the changing profile of patients undergoing catheter-based pulmonary embolism treatment: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract: PURPOSE: Despite growing evidence supporting pulmonary embolism response teams (PERT) in high-income countries, published experience from Latin America remains scarce. We assessed the association between PERT implementation and 30-day clinical outcomes in patients with acute PE treated with catheter-based therapy (CBT) in a Latin American university hospital. METHODS: Retrospective cohort study including consecutive patients with confirmed acute PE treated with CBT between 2004 and 2025. Patients were stratified by treatment era (pre-PERT: 2004-2020; PERT: 2021-2025). The primary endpoint was 30-day major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as a composite of all-cause death, stroke, or major bleeding (BARC grade ≥3). RESULTS: A total of 53 patients were included: 26 (49%) pre-PERT and 27 (51%) PERT era. ESC high-risk patients predominated in the pre-PERT era (17 (65%) vs 6 (22%); p = 0.002), while intermediate-high risk predominated in the PERT era (9 (35%) vs 21 (78%); p = 0.002). Dedicated thrombectomy devices were used universally in the PERT era (14 (54%) vs 27 (100%); p < 0.001). MACE occurred in 10 (38%) vs 4 (15%) patients (p = 0.06). In a subanalysis restricted to intermediate-high risk patients, 30-day mortality was 0/21 (0%) in the PERT era versus 3/9 (33%) in the pre-PERT era (p = 0.021). CONCLUSIONS: In one of the few Latin American reports on PERT-guided CBT, implementation was associated with a shift toward intermediate-high risk patients, greater use of mechanical thrombectomy, and lower thrombolytic exposure, without an increase in major bleeding. Among intermediate-high risk patients, 30-day mortality was significantly lower in the PERT era, supporting the safety and potential benefit of structured multidisciplinary PE management in resource-limited settings.

We assessed the association between PERT implementation and 30-day clinical outcomes in patients with acute PE treated with catheter-based therapy (CBT) in a Latin American university hospital. METHODS: Retrospective cohort study including consecutive patients with confirmed acute PE treated with CBT between 2004 and 2025.

title: Epigenome-Wide Association Study of Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Identifies Central Role for Inflammatory Pathways.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Epigenetic mechanisms underlying susceptibility to abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) remain poorly understood. Identifying causal DNA methylation markers for AAA can elucidate the regulatory processes that drive aneurysm formation and accelerate translational applications. We leveraged the Veterans Affairs (VA) Million Veteran Program to identify methylation biomarkers and delineate underlying pathways. METHODS: We first conducted an epigenome-wide association study of incident AAA (1324 cases and 42 065 noncases), performed stratified analyses by population group and smoking status, and conducted Mendelian randomization to facilitate causal inference of the cytosine-phosphate-guanine (CpG)-AAA association. Chromatin state, island context, and transcription factor binding were implicated through functional annotation of identified CpGs. To identify genes impacted by change in methylation state, we aligned associations with transcriptional data obtained in blood, aorta, and liver. We performed expression quantitative trait methylation to capture CpG-gene-expression links across the genome. Network Mendelian randomization was used to test cardiometabolic and inflammatory mediation. Finally, we developed a methylation risk score for AAA using penalized regression and evaluated its performance against a clinical model in the Million Veteran Program and 2 external studies. RESULTS: AGER, C2 DDR1 LDLR TRIB1 Epigenome-wide association study identified 1253 CpGs associated with incident AAA, and Mendelian randomization supported a putative causal role for 143 of these associations. Functional annotation pointed to predominantly distal, enhancer-centered regulation and enrichment of inflammatory transcription factor programs (eg, activator protein-1 and nuclear factor κB). This distal architecture was consistent with expression quantitative trait methylation results, which showed a larger number of trans associations. Among 143 CpGs associated with AAA in Mendelian randomization analyses, we identified 213 CpG-gene expression pairs with strong colocalization support, including, and. Multi-trait colocalization further prioritized 8 CpG-gene expression-AAA links with evidence of a shared genetic signal. Network Mendelian randomization identified 135 putative mediation pathways linking CpGs to AAA, including 58 via cardiometabolic traits and 77 via inflammation-related traits. Blood lipid traits mediated >40% of the associations between AAA risk and CpGs near(cg19305903) and(cg14128479). Among inflammation-related mediators, circulating DAG1, NEXN, MMP9, IL1RN, and MMP13 were prioritized as potential intermediates. Additionally, a CpG selection process was used to develop a methylation risk score for AAA, which strongly associated with disease in both the discovery cohort and 2 external validation cohorts, even after adjustment for a full suite of clinical covariates. CONCLUSIONS: This study identified putative causal DNA methylation markers for AAA, and multi-omics analyses implicate activator protein-1-linked inflammatory transcriptional programs, blood lipids, and multiple inflammation-related proteins as key pathways underlying methylation-associated AAA risk.

We leveraged the Veterans Affairs (VA) Million Veteran Program to identify methylation biomarkers and delineate underlying pathways.
